items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, says its customers won't bear the cost of a hack that hit its systems on November 2.
- Loss estimates differ: the exchange says about $38 million, Hypernative more than $40 million, Arkham at least $46 million and Chainalysis about $49 million.
- Deposits and withdrawals remain suspended with no restart date, days after a $6 billion theft at Binance that the FBI blamed on North Korea.
Brazil's largest crypto exchange says its users won't pay for its hack. Mercado Bitcoin, which lost tens of millions of dollars on Monday, says the losses are its problem, not its customers'.
An exchange holds your coins the way a bank holds your cash, and when one gets robbed, the customers are often the ones left waiting to see what they get back.
The exchange spotted a breach early on November 2 and froze deposits and withdrawals. “We identified and quickly contained a security incident in one of our systems early this morning,” Mercado Bitcoin said in a Portuguese-language statement on X. “As a preventive protection measure, deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended.”
It said no customer lost money and no data leaked. It has not said how the attackers got in.
How much was taken depends on who is counting. Security firm Hypernative flagged more than $40 million in suspicious transfers across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron.
Olá.
Primeiro, o mais importante: os ativos dos clientes estão garantidos . Os saldos continuam registrados nas respectivas contas.
Ontem (2/11), identificamos um incidente de segurança. Acionamos na hora nossos protocolos de segurança e governança e informamos as autoridades.…
— Mercado Bitcoin (@MercadoBitcoin) November 3, 2026
The exchange's own number is lower. “Right now the value of the assets involved is about $38 million,” Mercado Bitcoin said in a Portuguese-language update on X. “After a quick action with the crypto community and strategic partners, including Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1 and Chainalysis, we have already blocked $11 million.”
Others put it higher. Blockchain analysts at Arkham traced at least $46 million, while Chainalysis says about $49 million, with nearly $10 million frozen. The exchange has not said whether its $38 million includes the frozen amount.
Tether, which issues the USDT stablecoin (a token pegged to the dollar), froze more than $4.5 million in USDT tied to the incident, CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X.
A freeze only stops the tokens from moving. It doesn't return them to their owner, which is why the exchange's promise to cover losses carries the weight here.
On October 29, hackers drained more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's biggest exchange, and the FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group. Mercado Bitcoin has not linked its incident to that attack.
Binance made the same pledge as Mercado Bitcoin. “Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users,” CEO Richard Teng wrote on X, adding that about 95% of the affected assets had been replenished.
Neither promise can be checked from the outside. A guarantee to cover losses is only as good as the money behind it, and exchanges don't have to show customers their books.
For now, Mercado Bitcoin deposits and withdrawals remain suspended with no restart date. The exchange says it will post updates on X and resume service once full security is restored.

items.content:
In brief
- Six more companies, including Amazon, Tesla and SpaceX, objected to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, according to its Nov. 2 notice.
- The total has climbed from nine on Oct. 15 to 56, and Apple is now one of the few megacap names not on the list.
- A timely objection bars the venue from listing a third-party tokenized version of a stock, though the venue can still list shares that issuers tokenize themselves.
Two of Elon Musk’s companies are now keeping their shares off OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.
Tesla and SpaceX are among six new objecting issuers listed in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Monday. Amazon, Netflix, Lam Research, and SoFi Technologies are the others. The additions bring the total to 56 companies.
The list stood at 50 in the venue’s Oct. 30 notice, when Nvidia, Costco, and Nike led the biggest batch yet. That followed 38 on Oct. 28, after Walmart joined, and nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.
Tesla and SpaceX merger officially announced by...?
The new names deepen the roster of megacap holdouts. Amazon, Tesla, and Netflix join Microsoft, Alphabet, and Nvidia, while SoFi, a fintech company that offers crypto trading, adds a company with its own stake in digital assets. SpaceX, which trades under the ticker SPCX, rounds out the batch.
Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party.
If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue.
OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.
To trade, users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable “soulbound” token that the venue’s smart contracts verify before every transaction.
Apple is now one of the few megacap names still missing from the list. And while objections bar OKXICE from listing third-party tokenized versions of a company’s stock, they don’t close every door.
The notice says the venue can also list shares tokenized by the issuers themselves, though it doesn’t identify any, and that tokenized stocks it offers aren’t restricted to trading on OKXICE alone.

items.author: Ryan Gladwin
items.content:
In brief
- North Korean hackers allegedly drained $6.3 billion from Binance last week, the largest crypto hack on record.
- Their methods range from getting hired under fake identities to poisoning code libraries and compromising third-party wallet infrastructure.
- AI is making these attacks more convincing, with deepfakes already showing up in fake interviews.
Hackers from North Korea are notoriously effective at stealing crypto, with one estimate attributing 60% of all losses last year to DPRK-linked groups. These hackers enlist several different vectors of attack, making it all the more difficult to spot them in the act.
Last week, it took just 20 minutes for alleged North Korean hackers to drain $6.3 billion from Binance, in what is the biggest crypto hack on record. The attackers compromised a Binance engineer's work computer through a fake job interview, used an internal AI tool to gain control of other engineers' computers, and then used stolen credentials to hijack an internal wallet signing service, the exchange said.
— Binance (@binance) November 3, 2026
In the past, North Korean hackers have been known to get hired at crypto companies under fake identities, attack through third-party infrastructure, and poison widely used code libraries. More recently, they've started using AI to make all of it more convincing.
Here are some examples of the methods that North Korean hackers are known to use in crypto attacks.
Fake employees
Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su told Decrypt in August 2025 that the exchange throws out suspected North Korean resumes every day, and that "almost all the large DPRK hacks," at the time, had involved a fake employee helping facilitate the attack.
Su said there were tell-tale signs in resumes that indicate the applicant was from North Korea, but the exchange was not willing to reveal the specifics on the red flags. Sometimes, though, malicious actors get through to the interview stage, where the attackers use deepfakes to change their face and voice.
"The only real good detection is that they almost always have a slow internet connection," he told Decrypt. "What's happening is that the translation and the voice changer are working during the call … that's why they are always delayed."
Those who do get hired tend to be suspiciously good at the job. Su said North Korean workers are often among a company's top performers, likely because several people may be sharing one role across time zones.
The threat has not let up. Binance said its security team detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases in 2026, using techniques ranging from fraudulent job interviews to fake video conferencing apps.
Fake job interviews
Attackers also flip the scam around and pose as recruiters to target people who already work at high-profile crypto companies. Often, the attacker will claim there's a video or audio issue during the interview and send the victim a link to update Zoom, which infects their device with malware
"The DPRK group will [also] try to schedule calls with the external-facing employees," Su told Decrypt. "Either as a DeFi project or investment firm. Worst yet, they'll be recruiting them for a high-level job, paying twice, three times as much, just to get them onto an interview."
This is how the Binance attack began, according to the exchange. In September, a Binance software engineer was approached through a legitimate job-hunting platform by someone posing as a project director, who set up two interviews. In the first, a purported HR representative built trust over a live video call by sharing a social media account full of personal photos and videos, an approach Binance called "more advanced and deceptive than previously seen."
In the second, held on a chat app, the engineer was told to download an "assignment" onto his work computer. The code repository contained previously unknown malware that ran during setup, swapped a legitimate developer tool for a malicious version and connected to an attacker-controlled server, evading Binance's security tools.
One North Korea-linked group infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries between roughly December 2025 and July 2026 using similar methods. It took funds or credentials from more than 7,000 crypto wallets and moved around $10.71 million to North Korea.
The group, known as WaterPlum or Contagious Interview, posed as AI, crypto, or NFT companies and set candidates a technical interview or coding task that required downloading malware-filled files. Some used AI face-swapping software during interviews before cutting their video and asking the candidate to do the same, blaming a bad connection.
Library poisoning
Binance's Su also told Decrypt that North Korean hackers poison public code libraries, ranking it as the second most common method of attack—behind fake employees.
Node Package Manager (NPM) packages are collections of reusable, open-source code that developers frequently use. Attackers can clone these packages and slip in a small line of malicious code while keeping its original function. That means that a victim could use this poisoned code library and not notice, with the malicious code embedding itself deeper over time as more is built on top of it.
In September 2025, software security firm ReversingLabs found two NPM packages that used Ethereum smart contracts to download malware, which the firm said it hadn't seen before. The packages were tied to a wider network of GitHub repositories, mostly branded as crypto trading bots, with thousands of commits and stars that ReversingLabs thinks were mostly faked.
The tactic formed part of a “sophisticated campaign” of malicious actors attempting to hack users via poisoned blockchain-related public code libraries, a vector of attack that Binance has previously attributed to North Korean hackers.
To counter the threat, Su said, Binance makes employees go through NPM libraries with a fine-tooth comb.
Tampered developer tools also played a part in the Binance hack. In June, a member of Binance's wallet DevOps team downloaded a tampered installation of Homebrew, a popular software installer, while trying to install an AI coding tool he had found through a search engine, the exchange said. Its security team caught the problem, replaced the device and rotated his credentials, but the incident exposed the engineer and his colleagues on the wallet infrastructure team to the attackers.
Infrastructure attacks
Before Binance, the unwanted record for the largest crypto hack belonged to Bybit, which lost $1.4 billion in February 2025. Cybersecurity firms revealed that North Korean hackers pulled off the attack by planting malicious code into the infrastructure of Safe—a crypto wallet provider used by the exchange.
The security firms said malicious JavaScript code was directly injected into Safe's online infrastructure. Though, it was unclear how the attackers managed to do this.
Bybit's infrastructure "was not compromised," the exchange told Decrypt, and the hack came purely because a third party was exploited.
The Binance attack targeted the exchange's own systems. On October 29, the attacker used stolen credentials to deploy a container and gain unauthorized access to an internal wallet signing service, which let it initiate transactions outside Binance's normal withdrawal process. On Ethereum, it used the signing service to exploit EIP-7702, a mechanism that lets an account delegate execution rights to a smart contract, giving an attacker-controlled contract partial control over a Binance hot wallet.
Those on-chain authorizations kept working even after Binance suspended withdrawals. Because the hot wallet used multi-party computation, there was no single private key Binance could use to revoke them quickly, the exchange said.
AI-powered scams
Every single one of the above mentioned attack vectors can be turbo-charged with artificial intelligence tools.
Early this year, Google warned of an AI-powered malware campaign targeting crypto companies coming from North Korea. Similarly, Binance's Su also mentioned that AI tools can be used to increase the effectiveness of attacks.
Concerns around AI-powered hacks have risen in recent months, with Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin saying in October that it's "plausible" AI could break encryption within the next two years. It came amid an explosion in AI-driven maths, with OpenAI claiming to have cracked a 90-year-old maths problem in a matter of days. Experts urged the industry to prepare for AI-powered attacks on encryption.
There are no confirmed reports of North Korean hackers using AI to break encryption. But given how quickly they've adopted AI elsewhere, the industry may have to prepare for that next.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- About 700 of France's 10,000 supermarkets were hit in October, and nine more countries reported fridge problems on Monday.
- France's CERT-FR ties the compromises to Danfoss and Copeland remote controllers, and no group has claimed responsibility.
- Italy's government was set to hold a cybersecurity meeting Tuesday as CERT-FR warns the campaigns are probably still ongoing.
Europe's freezers have gone rogue, with supermarkets in nine more countries reporting refrigeration systems that heated up overnight on Monday.
Stores in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal and Sweden reported problems, and Estonian units were pushed to 50°C (122 °F).
No group has claimed responsibility, so the only ones taking the heat are the freezers.
The outbreak has a patient zero in France, where Finance Minister Roland Lescure told Parliament on Oct. 13 that about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets were affected.
#1 Searched Person on Google 2026?
According to France's CERT-FR, hackers forced a continuous defrost cycle, which spoiled food and sparked fires at some stores. CERT-FR said it was aware of numerous compromises of remote control modules made by Danfoss and Copeland.
Groupement Mousquetaires, which owns Intermarché and Netto, counted 300 stores affected, while Cooperative U said 80 of its 2,000 shops were hit. Lescure said food supplies were not at risk but acknowledged the attack "touches the heart of our food security." Some Mousquetaires display cases were still out of service that Tuesday.
Monday's wave hit several chains in Belgium, where Carrefour reported disruption at about 15 of its 700 stores. Sabcobel, a Belgian refrigeration contractor, said evaporators had been switched into defrost mode, and federal prosecutors opened an investigation. Four Delhaize outlets in Luxembourg also reported problems.
Italy's Radenza Group, which runs Coop-branded stores in Sicily, said the attack began at 4 a.m local time. and targeted the remote-control system for frozen food sections. Ireland's Musgrave counted 13 SuperValu stores affected, and Mosqueteiros confirmed incidents at seven Intermarché stores in Portugal.
At 50°C (122 °F), a freezer is well past hot-tub territory and turns basically into a low-powered steam oven or, worse, a bacteria incubator where germs grow quickly if food is left there too long.
In Sweden, Coop said six of its roughly 800 stores were hit and that they ran on 4G connections, making them "more exposed." Ica said a limited number of stores had problems and that the affected shops used an external Danfoss control system. Neither chain has confirmed a cyberattack, and Finland's Kesko says network interference has not been ruled out.
EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen called the incidents a "deliberate attempt" to disrupt the food supply chain. Investigators have not said whether Monday's wave is linked to the French attack.
Estonian refrigeration firm Kitman Coldtech said the affected units were older Danfoss models similar to those attacked in France. CERT-FR warns that leaving an end-of-life device without security patches exposed to the internet carries a very high risk of compromise. Researchers at Claroty published flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers in August, including an authentication bypass.
Claroty found 2,765 of those devices exposed online, and Danfoss fixed the flaws in firmware R4.3.1. It remains unclear which weaknesses the attackers used, and CERT-FR says the campaigns are probably still ongoing, while Italy's government was set to hold a cybersecurity meeting on Tuesday.
For now, CERT-FR advises operators to take the controllers off the public internet, and Sabcobel's CEO says many older units need physical modifications that require investment. Until those arrive, there is no real fix for the oldest units, which makes your 1998 chest freezer the most secure device on the continent.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Yohan Yun
items.content:
Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen
Markus Thielen sees Bitcoin reaching $90,000 by year-end, questions institutional ETF demand and says Ethereum must do more for holders.
Bitcoin’s days of consecutive double-digit price surges are over as Wall Street traders and profit-taking whales reshape the market, according to 10x Research founder Markus Thielen.
Institutional traders selling call options after rallies have made Bitcoin’s violent price explosions of earlier years less common, Thielen says in the latest episode of Cointelegraph’s Trade Secrets.
Thielen is also the author of Crypto Titans, a history of the industry. Writing the book led him to notice how each cycle brought different people pitching crypto to investors.
“Every cycle had actually different promoters, and different promoters bring in different investors,” he says.
This time, the promoters come from Wall Street, where investors trade on economic data and Federal Reserve decisions. Thielen says he expects Bitcoin will rise quickly on news, then spend time crab walking across the chart before the next big macro event.
Who’s really buying Bitcoin?
Thielen estimates that market makers account for up to half of the $60 billion in net spot Bitcoin ETF inflows he analyzed. Those firms hold ETF shares as a way to hedge their options trades, so the positions do not necessarily represent a bet that Bitcoin’s price will rise.
“So in the end it was not outright buying,” he says.
His estimate draws on a review of Form 13F filings, which disclose certain securities holdings of investment managers.
Thielen says the first wave of funds into the ETFs also included retail investors buying through institutions and corporate vehicles. Some paid substantial premiums to the value of the underlying crypto holdings.
“I would still think the institutions could come. I would still think that some of the sovereign wealth funds could come,” Thielen says.
Bitcoin could reach $90,000 by year-end
Thielen still sees Bitcoin reaching $90,000 by year-end. He says a drop into the mid-to-high $70,000s could come first.
Bitcoin has already been trading in that range, falling to about $76,100 on Friday following Binance’s $6.3 billion hack. BTC finished October down 7.3%, according to Coinglass.
Thielen compares the recovery in prices over recent months with early 2023, when Bitcoin rose from around $20,000 to $30,000. He says the doubts surrounding this year’s rebound are familiar as investors scan for the next price drop and entry point.
“I think everybody sort of missed it. So everybody wants to buy again.”
BTC’s return to $90,000 may rest partly on how much further the Fed raises borrowing rates. The central bank increased its benchmark rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September, to a target range of 3.75%–4%.
It held rates steady last Wednesday in a split vote, with two officials voting for another quarter-point increase. The Fed’s statement said inflation was still elevated, leaving open the possibility of further increases.
Thielen expects another hike by December, followed by a more cautious approach to further increases that could help Bitcoin rally toward year-end.
Ethereum needs to show holders the money
Thielen expects Bitcoin to outperform Ether, saying too much of the value from Ethereum activity goes to layer-2 networks.
“I look at it more as like a valuable utility, but nobody wants to pay for it.”
Making those networks cheaper to use has been a deliberate part of Ethereum’s development. But cheaper transactions may muddy the investment pitch for ETH.
Ethereum burns base fees paid by users, removing those coins from circulation. Its supply shrinks when the amount burned exceeds new ETH issued to validators. Lower fees can mean less ETH is destroyed.
ETH supply grows when issuance exceeds the amount burned. Source: ultrasound.money
Thielen, who says he has been bearish on Ether for more than a year, compares Ethereum with a highway.
“Everybody wants the highway to be empty so you can go fast, and the roads need to be super, super clean and fixed and everything, but nobody wants to pay for it,” he says.
He singles out Hyperliquid as an example of how trading activity can fund token purchases. The decentralized perpetuals exchange’s assistance fund converts trading fees into HYPE, which is then burned.
For Ethereum, he wants a stronger connection between the network’s use and the financial benefit to holders.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Binance traces $6.3B hack to fake job interviews, compromised AI tool
Hackers exploited compromised employee computers and stolen credentials to breach Binance’s wallet infrastructure, according to the exchange’s investigation.
A coding assignment from a prospective employer seemed like an ordinary part of a job interview. Instead, it was one step in a months-long cyberattack that ended with $6.3 billion stolen from Binance, raising questions about how exchanges protect themselves against threats that target their employees.
The attack was part of a coordinated campaign that exploited both human vulnerabilities and internal security systems, according to a postmortem released by Binance on Tuesday. The exchange’s findings detailed how hackers gradually gained access to its wallet infrastructure before the Oct. 29 theft.
How hackers infiltrated Binance
According to Binance’s security report, the attack campaign began in June, when an engineer downloaded a tampered software package while setting up an AI coding tool. Although Binance detected the malware and replaced the affected device, the attackers had already gathered information about the exchange’s wallet team.
In September, attackers posing as recruiters targeted another software engineer and tricked the employee into downloading a malicious file disguised as a coding assignment. The malware compromised the engineer’s work computer and evaded the exchange’s security protections.
On Oct. 20, the attackers used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain access to two additional engineers’s systems, obtaining deployment credentials that allowed them to install malicious software within Binance’s wallet infrastructure on Oct. 29.
The attackers then gained access to the exchange’s internal wallet-signing service, which authorizes cryptocurrency transactions. This allowed them to move funds outside the normal withdrawal process.
“This wasn’t one mistake or one breach — it was a months-long campaign,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in a Tuesday post on X.
Source: Richard Teng
Binance said the attackers also exploited Ethereum’s EIP-7702 mechanism, which allows wallets to delegate transaction permissions to smart contracts, enabling unauthorized transfers to continue even after the exchange suspended withdrawals. Its multiparty computation (MPC) wallet system, which distributes control over transaction signing, complicated efforts to revoke those permissions.
The breach affected approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets, with Binance reporting that $2.85 billion had been frozen or intercepted, according to its latest accounting. The exchange said it would absorb the losses rather than pass them on to customers and had replenished 98% of the affected token assets as of Oct. 31.
The attack, the largest cryptocurrency hack in history, has been attributed to North Korean hackers by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). On Tuesday, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied the country’s involvement, saying the FBI’s attribution was politically motivated and intended to damage North Korea’s international standing.
Binance reports 57 cyber threats blocked this year
Binance co-founder Yi He said Tuesday that the exchange’s security team had detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threats in 2026, including fraudulent job interviews, malicious software packages and social engineering attempts aimed at stealing credentials or installing malware.
“We intercepted many of them, but the cost of failing to stop even one was severe—and this should never have happened,” she said.

items.content:
Yesterday's hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper (OK, the authors classify is as a "blog post", but it's paper-shaped) found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model - literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers. I've been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I'm delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well!

Weight-Space Programming

Here's the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights:

Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.

Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights. With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x.

All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming.

The paper combines two topics that I think deserve to be treated separately. The first is what models can do with raw weights without running tools or executing code. The second explores how well models, once armed with code, can run operations to update and improve other models.

spaCy author Matthew Honnibal called the paper misleading for conflating the two, and Sean Goedecke deconstructed the Qwen3.5-0.8B update example as taking the same steps that a human ML researcher would use.

I'm going to focus on the no-tools question, which I think is the more interesting of the two.

The paper presents the first question as Can LLMs understand model behaviors from weights? They trained four neural networks to play simplified 10x10 grid versions of four classic computer games - Breakout, Pong, Pac-Man, and Freeway (I had to look that one up, it's an Atari 2600 game from 1981). Then they fed those weights (as floating point numbers) to an LLM along with the following question:

The weights below belong to one policy network that was trained with reinforcement learning to play a game on this grid. Which game was it trained on? Work from the weights. You have no tools: no code execution, no calculator, nothing to run. This is a single response.

The GitHub repository that accompanies the paper is RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs. The exp1_which_game folder contains the prompts they used, with weights for the four games:

  • breakout/prompt.txt
  • freeway/prompt.txt
  • pacman/prompt.txt
  • pong/prompt.txt

I checked and, aside from the weights, each prompt is identical to the others.

Trying it out with Qwen 3.8 27B and other models

The prompts on GitHub are self-contained. My LLM tool has a -f/--fragment option which can be passed the URL to a text file to use as a prompt, which means I can run any of the above like this:

llm -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs/refs/heads/main/exp1_which_game/runs/breakout/prompt.txt \
  -m openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro

This example requires the llm-openrouter plugin installed, and runs the Breakout prompt against Kimi K3.1 Pro via OpenRouter. Here's what I got back from Kimi K3.1 Pro, which successfully guessed Breakout after 9m 41s and 19,493 reasoning tokens.

But how about Qwen 3.8 27B? That's still my favorite model to run on my own laptop - it's just 17GB (I use this version) and somehow feels close to the leading proprietary models of 2025.

I fired up LM Studio, ensured Qwen 3.8 27B was loaded with a long context window (the default 8192 context failed with errors), installed the llm-lmstudio plugin and ran this command:

LMSTUDIO_TIMEOUT=900 \
  llm -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs/refs/heads/main/exp1_which_game/runs/pacman/prompt.txt \
  -m lmstudio/qwen/qwen3.8-27b

(I had to bump the timeout up using an environment variable, see this issue.)

After 46m 12s and 43,506 reasoning tokens, Qwen on my laptop returned a response that ended like this (here's the reasoning trace):

Game: A simplified Pac-Man-style gridworld: an agent moves through a fixed 8x8 maze with central and corner wall blocks, moving objects/ghosts, and reward targets/pellets.

Description: The agent navigates a fixed maze-like 8x8 board, using current agent/moving-object/previous-frame cues to move through corridors, collect reward-target cells, and avoid moving objects or hazards.

Confidence: 72%

This is impressive. I tried it on two of the other games as well. It identified Pong (reasoning) in 1h 4m 54s:

Pong — specifically a Pong-like paddle/ball game where the agent controls a vertical paddle on the right side and must move up/down to intercept or return a moving ball/reward object.

Description:

The agent moves a right-side paddle vertically to hit or catch a moving ball-like reward target moving across the 8×8 field, while a left-side moving object/opponent and wall borders define the play; reward is obtained by successfully intercepting/returning/scoring the ball, and missing or failing to hit it is penalized.

Confidence:

75%

And Breakout (reasoning) in 52m 25s:

Game: Breakout, or an Arkanoid-like paddle/ball/brick game.

Description: The agent is a paddle on the bottom row and moves left/right to keep a ball in play; the ball moves around the upper grid, and bricks/reward targets in the top rows give reward when hit, while missing the ball/hitting the bottom wall ends the episode or gives penalty.

Confidence: 88%

Qwen failed at the Freeway prompt, which didn't surprise me considering that game is more obscure than the other three. Here's that transcript - Qwen thought it was "A simplified Pac-Man-like grid game: agent moves 4-directionally".

The reasoning traces are fun to skim, and almost incomprehensible. Here's a sample:

What about agent channel0? We see some large channel0 rows near row8 col7/8 and maybe bottom? Let's list channel0 large: line436 input435 (row8 col7 ch0) -2.107,1.169,0.513...; line441 input440 (row8 col8 ch0) -0.376,0.010,1.564,3.855...; line445 input444 (row8 col8 ch4) 0.142,0.491...; line382? input381 ch0? Wait line382 input381: 381//5=76 (row7 col6), ch1? 381%5=1? 76 * 5=380, ch1. So not. Channel0 large maybe at row8 col7/8 only. Also top row? line44 input43 ch3, line49 ch3. Channel0 large maybe not many. Agent position could be near bottom-right? If the agent is typically at bottom-right?

That said though, I expect a sufficiently experienced human being armed with a notepad and a pencil could get there with enough effort.

It's a cool paper, but some of the wider commentary I've seen around it does not feel justified. I'm not ready to declare that the age of source code is over and our future involves incomprehensible machines editing their own model weights in incomprehensible ways.

items.content:
In brief
- The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said critical infrastructure should be braced for a ransomware attack involving AI-powered malware by 2028.
- NCSC chief Richard Horne warned that AI will expose vulnerabilities tolerated "for far too long," and said the era of "tech on the cheap" must end.
- The warning comes as the UK puts £60 million into a national Cyber Shield and £70 million into a new center to find vulnerabilities in critical systems.
Britain's critical national infrastructure should be braced for a ransomware attack involving AI-powered malware by 2028, the UK's National Cyber Security Centre warned on Tuesday.
Within the next two years, hostile actors' use of AI is "highly likely" to increase the scale and efficiency of their operations, including ransomware, social engineering and the exploitation of software vulnerabilities, according to the NCSC's annual State of the Cyber Nation report. The agency is part of GCHQ, the UK's signals intelligence service.
Today, we've published our 2026 annual review: The State of the Cyber Nation.
The UK faces a moment of choice. The future of cyber resilience is not set.
Read the report now:https://t.co/TzqzYedqXQ@GCHQ @DanJarvisMBE pic.twitter.com/mIFWrBB5Yt
— NCSC UK (@NCSC) November 3, 2026
The threat stems less from new attack techniques than from old weaknesses, NCSC chief executive Richard Horne said in prepared remarks for a speech launching the report.
"In the coming months, we face a real prospect of an unprecedented rise in the number of cyber incidents," Horne said. "But we must be clear that is not because AI has invented new ways to attack us. But because vulnerabilities that have been tolerated for far too long can now be discovered and exploited at a scale that was once unimaginable."
"For decades, we have collectively got away with doing tech on the cheap," he added.
Horne urged organizations to invest properly in their technology, stop connecting systems to the internet unnecessarily, and treat the government's Cyber Essentials certification as the starting point for their security rather than the end goal. Leaders who fail to act could have to explain to investors, staff and customers why "food isn't on shelves, lights aren't on, businesses have gone under," he warned.
The government last week announced £60 million (about $80 million) for the first phase of a national Cyber Shield, £70 million ($93 million) for a new National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre to identify weaknesses across critical infrastructure, and a new AI Cyber Security Centre of Excellence in Manchester, run by the NCSC.
AI and cyberattacks
The warning follows growing evidence that attackers are already putting AI to work. In May, Google's Threat Intelligence Group said cybercriminals had used an AI model to find and weaponize a previously unknown flaw that let them bypass two-factor authentication in a popular open-source administration tool, the first time it had confirmed AI-assisted zero-day development in the wild. A Cambridge University study of more than 90,000 cybercrime forum threads published the same month, however, found that most criminals were using AI for spam and phishing rather than sophisticated attacks.
UK officials have sounded the alarm before. In July, Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper warned that governments must agree on AI safeguards before frontier systems transform warfare, crime and society. "We cannot afford to wait for an AI equivalent of Hiroshima before we act," she wrote.

items.content:
Bitcoin price defends $76K lows as analysts see stocks pricing in ‘political gridlock’
Bitcoin made modest gains at the start of Wall Street trading on Tuesday as markets awaited cues from the US midterm elections.
Bitcoin (BTC) headed higher at Tuesday’s Wall Street open as a tech-stock rebound under the shadow of uncertainty surrounding the US midterm elections.
Key points:
- Bitcoin price action edged 0.7% higher on Tuesday as US equities avoided succumbing to midterm election uncertainty.
- Analysis from The Kobeissi Letter suggested markets were pricing in two years of political uncertainty amid expectations of Democratic gains in the midterm elections.
- WTI crude oil dipped to $93.59 per barrel, its lowest level since Oct. 15, despite fresh US strikes targeting Iran’s Qeshm Island.
BTC price volatility cools as stocks rise
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD circling $77,000, continuing to retain local lows near $76,300 seen on Friday.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Stocks faced conflicting forces at the start of the US trading session. Apple shares sought to pare losses after falling 4% in premarket trading as the company forecast gross margins of 45% to 46% for the December quarter, down from 47.9% in the previous quarter, citing rising memory-chip costs.
Markets also weighed the potential impact of the US midterm elections on the balance of power in Congress. Although polls suggested significant Democratic gains, some analysts cautioned that the results could be less decisive than expected.
Apple stock one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
“Investors seem to have a significant dose of skepticism about whether the final outcome is going to be quite as favorable to Democrats as the polling suggests,” Tobin Marcus, head of US policy and politics at equity research company Wolfe Research, told CNBC. Wolfe added that polls were “likely overstating Democratic strength.”
The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index finished Monday down 0.5% and 1.1%, respectively. Analysts at trading resource The Kobeissi Letter argued that US political uncertainty, rather than concerns over AI spending alone, was driving market weakness.
“The reality is that the market is pricing-in a major shift in the political landscape of the US,” it wrote on X.
The analysis suggested that a divided Congress could lead to frequent legislative impasses, creating conditions in which policy decisions would become less predictable.
“A change in the political landscape always comes with uncertainty; markets hate uncertainty,” it continued.
“Objectively, the market is in the process of pricing-in two years of political gridlock.”
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Related: Bitcoin price threatens $77.7K support loss with recent buyers underwater
Oil digests latest Iran strike after 7% drop
Oil prices meanwhile brushed off a US attack on Iran’s Qeshm Island, a key military control outpost for the Strait of Hormuz oil route.
The move came just days after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that President Donald Trump was open to resolving the US-Iran war “diplomatically,” comments that triggered a 7% drop in WTI crude oil on Monday.
WTI initially jumped to $98.80 per barrel before dipping below $94 on Tuesday, hitting its lowest level since Oct. 15.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

items.author: Bennett Tomlin
items.content:
First Digital Trust, the firm behind the FDUSD stablecoin, announced early last month that it had signed a business combination agreement that would result in it being publicly listed, with a closing expected next year.
The announcement comes after the market capitalization of its flagship product, FDUSD, collapsed, losing over $4 billion since its peak in April 2024.
Binance is in a good position to benefit from this public listing, as a Binance-related entity, Alphanest Holdings, is a major warrant holder in this firm.
Alphanest is currently owned by Binance Holdings (IE) Limited and was previously owned by Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who was recently released from prison.
This warrant, if executed, will result in this Binance entity holding approximately one-quarter of the equity in this firm after the merger.
In anticipation of this potential merger and in light of the recent difficulties for both First Digital and Binance, Protos took a deep dive into the finances and information that have been shared so far.
Falling revenue, growing loss
The market cap collapse of FDUSD is only one of the financial difficulties that First Digital Trust is facing, with its revenue also falling substantially. The firm will have a pre-money valuation of $250 million for this merger.
First Digital’s provided investor presentation shows that for fiscal year 2025 (which it concluded on June 30, 2025), it had $87 million in revenue, and for its unaudited 2026 revenue (which presumably also ended in June), it has merely $27 million.
Even worse than that, the chart shows that for 2025 it had a net revenue of $6 million, $10 million more than the net revenue loss of $4 million for 2026.
Its adjusted operating loss also increased from $17 million to $19 million.
As it notes, “FDUSD revenue is driven by reserves in cash and equivalents,” and since the market capitalization of its stablecoin has been falling, we would also expect its returns from that stablecoin’s reserves.
This problem is compounded by the fact that the supply of FDUSD has fallen by approximately another $50 million since June 30.
It’s holdings are also intensely concentrated in Binance-labeled wallets, with approximately 90% of the FDUSD on Ethereum being in Binance-labeled addresses. This represents approximately $170 million in value and is replicated across chains.
On Sui, there are approximately $43 million FDUSD in a Binance-labeled wallet.
Protos believes approximately 80% of all FDUSD is held in Binance wallets.
Fighting with Justin Sun
First Digital Trust’s investor relations page lists its defamation lawsuit against Justin Sun as a material legal proceeding for the firm.
This lawsuit is in response to Sun’s allegations about the firm.
Sun and Techteryx — a firm related to TrueUSD — had previously sued First Digital Trust over allegations that First Digital had misappropriated the reserves for TrueUSD.
Read more: TUSD up to 99.7% backed by speculative assets despite SEC settlement
Sun went beyond the allegations in that lawsuit and also took to X to air out his claim that “It’s evidently the case that First Digital Trust(FDT) is unable to fulfill client fund redemptions and effectively insolvent.”
This led to First Digital initially stating on X that “every FDUSD is securely backed 1:1 by cash and cash equivalents” and adding that the firm “remains fully solvent.”
Subsequently, First Digital filed its suit against Sun.
Read more: First Digital defends FDUSD from Justin Sun’s attacks
First Digital has also recently settled with Archblock and TrueCoin, two of the firms that previously operated TrueUSD, as part of the Archblock bankruptcy.
Techteryx has filed for a Chapter 11 trustee to be appointed in the Archblock bankruptcy case.
It accuses Archblock of “ultimately defrauding Techteryx for the benefit of a corrupt set of foreign purported investment entities, which in turn paid lucrative commissions to the fraud’s participants.”
Techteryx is trying to allude to its allegations that Legacy Trust (a somewhat-precursor vehicle to First Digital) and First Digital had misappropriated TrueUSD reserves by directing them to the Aria Fund.
Binance, which recently was hacked for several billion dollars worth of value, could soon become a major shareholder in a publicly-listed stablecoin issuer.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Aztec, the privacy-focused Ethereum layer-2, launched its Aztec Tierra upgrade, fixing a critical vulnerability and adding security hardening.
- A new architecture cuts Ethereum-to-Aztec message delivery from two minutes to as low as 12 seconds.
- It arrives with private apps spanning payments, trading, AI and social—led by the revived zk.money—amid a broader Ethereum privacy push.
Aztec, the privacy-focused Ethereum layer-2 network, has rolled out a major upgrade that fixes a critical vulnerability from its previous version, doubles the speed of private transactions, and ushers in a wave of applications built to keep user data hidden.
The Aztec Foundation said Tuesday that the upgrade, called Aztec Tierra and designated Alpha V6, delivers stronger security, formal verification of its proving system and faster deposits from Ethereum, alongside a refreshed brand.
Aztec is a decentralized layer-2 with more than 3,000 validators and fully programmable private smart contracts, and it pitches itself as having no privileged viewing keys or centralized sequencer, meaning no single operator can peer into or control user activity.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
The upgrade resolves known vulnerabilities from earlier versions, including a critical issue discovered in V5, and adds extensive hardening. Notably, that includes a new AI-powered security testing harness and formal verification of core cryptographic components, a mathematical process for proving code behaves as intended.
The move reflects a broader scramble across crypto to harden code as AI tools make vulnerabilities easier to find.
On performance, Aztec said private transactions now generate client-side proofs in about one second on a standard device, twice as fast as before, while a new architecture cuts the time for Ethereum-to-Aztec messages from an average of two minutes to as little as 12 seconds, speeding up deposits and cross-chain activity.
“Privacy shouldn’t be something you have to request or trust someone else to protect,” said Zac Williamson, co-founder and CEO of the Aztec Foundation. “It should be built into the network.”
The upgrade arrives with a crop of private applications spanning payments, trading, AI and social.
Leading them is zk.money, a private payments and savings app built by Aztec Labs that the team revived this year. With Tierra’s faster messaging, users can deposit directly from any Ethereum wallet without complex bridging.
Others in the lineup include Galactica for private AI inference, Nemi for private perpetuals trading, a private browser wallet called Nulo, and Rolling Chat, a private message board based on Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s own Aztec experiments.
The launch lands amid a renewed push for privacy on Ethereum. Buterin has laid out plans for a “cryptographic world computer” and pressed to slash the cost of quantum-safe privacy, while a separate team spun out a for-profit firm to drive institutional privacy adoption.
Aztec, which raised $17 million in an earlier funding round to build out its network, is betting that privacy becomes a default feature of Ethereum rather than an add-on.

items.content:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors fall further as outflows continue; BTC at $77.3k
- BTC ETFs see another $400M in outflows, now $1B+ since Binance hack
- Kim Jong Un’s sister says NK not involved in Binance hack and calls allegations a “provocation”
- Tom Lee calls Binance hack “constructive,” points to no socialized losses & no DeFi blow-ups
- Strategy buys $65M of BTC last week and $208M of STRC
🐂 Tom Lee Calls the Binance Hack Bullish for Ethereum
Tom Lee looked at the largest crypto theft ever recorded and called the market’s response “constructive”. His company, BitMine Immersion, bought another 8,573 ETH last week, roughly $19.6 million worth, lifting the treasury to 6,060,506 ETH and about $13.7 billion. That’s 4.9% of the total circulating ETH supply, which makes Lee the most ETH-exposed executive on the planet.
His case comes down to one comparison. ETH fell about 4% after the $6.3 billion Binance hack. After the Bybit hack in February 2025, it dropped 8% on day one and 20% over the following week. Lee called that “relatively muted crypto market reaction very constructive” and read it as proof the industry can take a hit this size without cracking.
He pointed to four things behind the bullishness:
- Binance covered the loss from its own balance sheet instead of socializing it
- Tether and Circle froze the stolen stablecoins within hours
- No DeFi protocol blew up as collateral damage, and
- Investigators pinned the attack on North Korea almost immediately.
Each of those is a thing that went right in 2026 and went badly in 2025.
The price read holds up, but there are bigger questions for ETH’s future from a trading perspective. October was the worst month in the history of U.S. spot ETH ETFs, with $1.61 billion in net outflows. ETH is down 19% from its local peak, opposed to 11& for Bitcoin.
A potential driver of ETH’s weakness is Tom Lee himself. BitMine is now 99% of the way to the 5% supply cap Lee has said the company will stop at, about 49,500 ETH short, roughly six weeks at last week’s pace. ETH has had a large, price-insensitive, weekly corporate buyer for most of a year, and that buyer is nearly finished.
Now we wait to see what the bid looks like without it. And if Tom Lee’s bullish read is the correct one…
🌎 Macro Crypto and Markets
- Crypto majors are slightly red as outflows continue; BTC -0.6% at $77.3k; ETH even at $2,280; SOL -1% at $93; HYPE -1% at $85; ZEC -3% at $1,210
- STX (+4%), WLFI (+2%), XMR (+3%) and PUMP (+4%) led top alt movers
- Oil -1% at $98; Gold even at $3,910
- Stock futures are mixed ahead of midterms; DOW -0.8%, Nasdaq +0.2%
- Brazil’s largest exchange Mercado Bitcoin halted deposits and withdrawals Monday after a security incident
- ZachXBT flagged more than $106 million drained from an unnamed EU entity’s exchange accounts on Sunday; he said with high confidence the thief is not Lazarus, and the money moved through ETH, Monero and cross-chain bridges within 24 hours
- BTCPay Server told merchants to shut down their instances Sunday after reports of attackers sweeping hot wallets with administrator access
- Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied Pyongyang had any role in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, calling the FBI’s attribution “absurd rhetoric” and a “grave political provocation” in state media
Corporate Treasuries & ETFs

items.author: Aaron Wise
items.content:
AI companies have announced over $200 billion worth of new cash borrowing and equity financing deals during the second half of this year despite the PHLX Semiconductor Sector shedding a quarter of its value in the same period.
Created in 1993 by the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, the PHLX Semiconductor Sector is a capitalization-weighted index made up of the 30 largest US-traded companies that design, distribute, manufacture, and sell semiconductors.
As stock prices across the AI sector have declined, executives have rushed to secure financing via capital raises. Among them, Oracle filed $20 billion worth of fresh debt and equity offerings this week, adding to a record-shattering $95 billion financing plan by Meta.
Microsoft joined in the borrowing spree, pricing a $25 billion bond on October 29 — the company’s first major US debt sale in nine years.
All of the biggest AI companies are borrowing at once. Alphabet (Gemini AI), SpaceX (Grok AI), Meta (Meta AI), Microsoft (CoPilot AI), along with Oracle, have announced $129 billion in combined financing since last week alone.
The inverse correlation between AI stock performance and fundraising by those same companies is particularly obvious since June 30, with a step-up in borrowing as share prices have crashed 27%, as measured by SOXQ, an ETF tracking the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index.
AI companies supercharge borrowing
On a year-to-date basis, AI hyperscalers have already borrowed at least $214 billion in 2026, already 157% more than the $83 billion they raised across all of 2025.
For example, Meta’s new financing plan from last Monday paired $35 billion of stock sales with a $60 billion at-the-market stock sale program.
Days earlier, Mark Zuckerberg’s company guided $135-145 billion worth of 2026 capital expenditures.
That’s mostly financing the company’s massive AI investments, with spending on compute and infrastructure dwarfing everything Meta plans to generate in operating cash flow this year.
Nebius, an AI neocloud company, closed a $5.75 billion convertible sale in August. Its communications chief called it one of the largest corporate convertibles in its history.
CoreWeave, a Jensen Huang-endorsed AI neocloud, issued $4.2 billion more convertible debt on September 22. Its total debt now exceeds $35 billion.
Five-year credit default swaps of CoreWeave breached a concerning 1,000 basis points in October, as credit investors view its likelihood of default rising.
Including off-balance-sheet commitments, hyperscalers’ aggregate obligations now sit near $3.5 trillion, per calculations from UBS.
Read more: Meta’s AI bond just hit a record low as its stock soared
Large drawdowns in AI stocks
As AI executives have raced to borrow more money, common shareholders have suffered declining confidence in business prospects. CoreWeave stock has declined 63% from its high this year. Nebius is down 53%.
Even the bluest of bluechips are delivering massive drawdowns.
From their peaks this year, Oracle has declined 55%, Meta 22%, Alphabet 31%, and Nvidia 17%.
Michael Burry, the investor who shorted subprime mortgages before 2008, has told subscribers that Nvidia’s more than $500 billion off-balance-sheet financing has “shades of Enron” and reads as “a sign of desperation.”

items.author: Ryan Gladwin
items.content:
In brief
- Binance has burned a share of its Luna Classic trading fees nearly every month since March 2023, but November’s burn has yet to arrive.
- Community members suspect the delay is tied to the record $6.3 billion hack of Binance, which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor.
- One prominent community member claims Binance is moving LUNC to a more secure wallet before resuming the burn, though Binance has not confirmed.
Centralized exchange Binance has burned Luna Classic tokens on the first of every month since 2023, when Do Kwon's Terra Luna empire came crumbling down. At the start of November, however, that burn has not occurred.
Luna Classic (LUNC) is the original native token for the Terra blockchain, which Terraform Labs founder Do Kwon forked and left behind in 2022 in a bid to rescue his collapsing project. Kwon was later convicted of fraud and sentenced to 15 years in prison for his role in Terra’s $40 billion implosion. Yet the decentralized network he left behind has kept running, propped up by a passionate community of supporters who have sunk time, effort and money into keeping it alive.
Binance started the burns after Terra Classic’s community voted to burn a portion of every on-chain LUNC transaction in late 2022, with the exchange pledging to burn half of the trading fees earned from the token. In practice, this has come in the form of a batch of burns happening at the start of every month since March 2023, but, according to StatsBin data, November's burn has yet to come in.
Some Luna Classic investors are concerned about Binance's lack of monthly burn, while others point to last week's record-breaking hack of the exchange as a reason behind the burn's delay.
"It is an important sign of support and a vital part of the overall burn campaign," Dawid Skinder, brand and user experience ecosystem contributor for Terra Classic, told Decrypt. "It might be that it is just an operational issue after the biggest hack ever. Hopefully that is the case, Terra Classic does not need another problem."
Binance was hacked for $6.3 billion on Friday, which the FBI has attributed to TraderTraitor—the North Korean group blamed for the Bybit hack. It has been labelled the biggest crypto hack in history, with estimated losses at four times the previous record of $1.5 billion from the Bybit heist.
The exchange has been reopening withdrawals on the platform in stages, with the latest taking place late on Monday for dozens of Ethereum and Solana tokens. Some investors have questioned whether the LUNC burn is a priority for the exchange as it attempts to recover from the hack.
Burn $LUNC and quit fucking around
— Tango and Cash (@ThisDud30190229) November 2, 2026
"Yes, the hack was a problem," prominent Luna Classic community member Pedro, better known as Vegas, told Decrypt. "At the moment, we are helping them to keep LUNC and LUNA safe."
He has long claimed to be in direct contact with Binance regarding LUNC issues, though this has yet to be verified. Vegas claims Binance is working on security maintenance after the hack and is moving LUNC to a more secure wallet before proceeding with the burn.
Binance did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.
The exchange has paused its LUNC burns once before, withholding contributions at the end of 2022 after the Terra Classic community voted to re-mint burned tokens as a development fund. Binance halved its burn to 50% of trading fees and only resumed in March 2023, once the community had scrapped the re-mints.
Luna Classic has dropped 7.9% in value over the past week to $0.0000417, per Decrypt data, and is down 99.99% from its all-time high of $119.18. Investors believe the Binance burn being paused is just one of many issues the token faces.
Skinder told Decrypt that Luna Classic needs to fix its lack of products, improve its marketing, conduct a proper audit, and protect itself against quantum attacks. Skinder said he believes in a revival but claims that it is difficult with decentralized governance and "amateur validators."
So, why bother? Why not spend time on another chain?
"There are X number of chains in a better state than Terra Classic. None of them (except Bitcoin, probably) have that history and narrative (biggest crypto revival ever). None of them have 20+ stablecoins that are waiting to be re-pegged and restored," Skinder said. "Low chance of success, big upside if done. Great history to be part of."

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- The Liquid Federation said the sidechain's Bitcoin reserves have been fully restored, reestablishing 1:1 backing for all LBTC after a September exploit.
- Purported white-hat hackers withdrew about 4,000 BTC from the federation wallet in September, returning 3,400 BTC but keeping around 598 BTC.
- Back said key systems have been hardened and audited, and urged developers to treat AI-suggested fixes "with suspicion."
The Liquid Network's Bitcoin reserves have been fully restored, two months after self-described white-hat hackers drained most of them, the Liquid Federation said on Monday.
The federation said it had reestablished 1:1 Bitcoin backing for all LBTC, the token that represents Bitcoin on Liquid. The milestone follows the restoration of swaps between BTC and LBTC at a 1:1 rate through participating providers several weeks ago, it said.
Update from the Liquid Federation:
The Liquid Federation is pleased to announce that the network’s bitcoin reserves have been fully restored, reestablishing 1:1 BTC backing for all LBTC.
This follows the restoration of BTC<>LBTC swaps several weeks ago, which have since allowed…
— Liquid Network 🌊 (@Liquid_BTC) November 3, 2026
Blockstream CEO Adam Back, whose company develops the technology behind Liquid, posted a screenshot of the network's dashboard showing assets matching liabilities at 100%, with a reserve deficit of 0.00 BTC. Users running their own Liquid nodes can verify the federation's reserves directly, the federation said.
It did not say how the shortfall left by the hack was covered.
Launched by Blockstream in 2018, Liquid is a Bitcoin sidechain, a separate blockchain that runs alongside Bitcoin, designed for faster and more private transfers. Users lock up BTC in a wallet controlled by the federation, a group of exchanges and other crypto companies that run the network, and receive the same amount of LBTC in return.
Asked on X what would stop a repeat of the hack, Back listed three hardened "lines of defense": refreshed peg-out authorization keys now held in cold hardware wallets, disabled proof validation caches along with a bug fix for nodes, and consensus rules that have been hardened to "fail closed." The network has also been through multiple third-party audits, he said.
"And lesson: treat with suspicion (don't trust, verify) AI suggested fixes," Back wrote.
Back had pointed to AI's growing role in security in an interview with Bloomberg Television on October 20, describing "a wave of AI-assisted security analysis" over the previous couple of months. "AI, of course, is a tool to help develop code and to secure the code, but also it can be used to find defects," he said, adding that it had been "affecting many companies in the sector." He said then that the hacked funds remained "under investigation."
The federation said it is modernizing Liquid's governance structure, introducing clearer responsibilities and oversight, and adding further technical and operational safeguards, with more details to come in the coming weeks.
The September exploit
On September 6, purported white-hat hackers withdrew about 4,000 BTC, then worth around $320 million, from Liquid's federation wallet, communicating with Blockstream through PGP-signed messages embedded in Bitcoin transactions.
The next day, they returned 3,400 BTC, worth about $269 million, after Blockstream said Liquid's bridge nodes had been patched, but kept roughly 598 BTC. Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet said that if the remaining coins were a negotiated reward, the arrangement looked "more like extortion than white-hat hacking."
Blockstream later refused to pay a ransom for the outstanding Bitcoin. "Taking assets without authorization and withholding their return is a crime, not responsible disclosure," the company said. "It is not white-hat activity. It is theft."

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- North Korea has denied it was behind the hack of Binance, with Kim Yo Jong calling U.S. accusations a "sinister" attempt to damage the country's image.
- The FBI, the Secret Service and blockchain analytics firms have attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group blamed for the Bybit hack.
- Binance said net withdrawals since Sunday reached $4.72 billion, but that hourly deposits began exceeding withdrawals late on Monday.
North Korea has rejected U.S. findings that it was behind the record hack of Binance, calling the FBI's attribution a "grave political provocation," Yonhap reported on Tuesday.
"It is a grave political provocation against the DPRK that the U.S. misleads the international public opinion as if all the cyber crimes in different parts of the world are our deeds," Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said in a statement carried by the state-run Korean Central News Agency. She called the accusation a "sinister" attempt to damage North Korea's international image.
Kim also turned the blame back on Washington, pointing to the Trump administration's plan to use confiscated crypto as a strategic reserve. Anyone who looks at who will end up with "the so-called stolen cryptocurrency" once it is retrieved "may get a clue about who is behind the hacking incident," she said.
The FBI said on Saturday that North Korean hackers it calls TraderTraitor were responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, confirming the attribution blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis made last week. The FBI attributed the $1.5 billion hack of crypto exchange Bybit in February 2025 to the same group. North Korea has denied previous accusations of hacking.
The hackers are moving their haul quickly. North Korea is laundering the funds at a rate of roughly one new wallet every 25 seconds, across about 12,000 wallets, Decrypt reported on Monday. About $2.85 billion of the $6.43 billion stolen has been frozen or seized, compared with roughly 3% of the funds taken from Bybit.
Not all of the stolen funds are moving at the same pace. As of Monday, more than $1 billion in ETH and about $1.42 billion in BTC had seen limited onward movement, while other funds were moving rapidly across chains, blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said. The activity so far is broadly consistent with the "immediate layering" phase seen after past North Korean hacks, though funds repeatedly returning to earlier addresses across thousands of transactions suggests automation, the firm said. It expects the scale of the theft to "strain the actors' trusted laundering channels," pushing funds toward bridges, instant exchanges and swapping services.
As of Nov 2, over $1B in ETH and ~$1.42 billion in BTC stolen from Binance have seen limited onward movement since the theft.
Other stolen funds are moving rapidly across chains.
These funds are not all progressing through the laundering process at the same pace. pic.twitter.com/ZEVCZzCDRM
— Chainalysis (@chainalysis) November 2, 2026
Binance's recovery
Binance did not respond to the BBC's questions about North Korea's alleged involvement. A company spokesperson told the outlet that a net $4.72 billion had been withdrawn since withdrawals resumed on Sunday, a "relatively limited portion" of total assets of about $157 billion.
By 10 p.m. ET on Monday, hourly deposits were exceeding withdrawals, "reflecting improving user activity and stabilizing flows," Binance tweeted. The exchange has since restored withdrawals for dozens more tokens on Ethereum and Solana.
Binance also said on Monday that users holding its 10 largest tokens, including BTC, ETH, USDT and USDC, can now verify that their balances are fully backed, using a zero-knowledge proof of its October 31 reserves snapshot. It has covered about 95% of the stolen assets, with the rest made up of less liquid tokens that take longer to buy, and plans to take a wider snapshot on Wednesday.

items.content:
Anthropic警告：AI可能很快进入自我加速阶段，等人类察觉或为时已晚

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 在 11 月 2 日更新的 IPO 招股书中警告，AI 可能很快跨过「递归自我改进」（RSI）相关的关键门槛，让 AI 研发速度大幅加快。过去也出现过未能及时察觉研发进步显著加速，直到加速发生后才发现的情况。

目前，Claude 已经参与编写代码、运行实验和处理训练数据，帮助开发更强的下一代模型。新模型又能反过来加快后续研发，形成不断提速的循环。

按照 Anthropic 的安全政策，触及这道关键门槛有两种情况：
1. AI 能以相近成本完成整个 AI 研究团队的工作；
2. 或者让 AI 技术进步速度至少翻倍，把原本需要两年取得的进步压缩到一年。

随着 AI 越来越深入自身研发，模型能力可能增长得比安全评测、对齐研究和防护措施的更新还快。Anthropic 目前尚未认定任何现有模型达到这一水平，此次预警主要基于内部估算和对未来模型的预测。目前正考虑修改安全政策，确保关键研发过程仍由人类监督和控制。

大摩警告电力超级周期被市场低估：2030年全球用电量将达36万亿度，亚洲贡献64%新增需求

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，摩根士丹利在最新研报中指出，全球电力需求增长正从单一的 AI 数据中心扩展至 AI、产业迁移和空调制冷三大驱动力，电力行业正迎来新一轮「超级周期」，但市场尚未充分定价这一趋势。

大摩将全球电力消费预测上调约 10%，预计到 2030 年全球用电量将达到 36 万亿度，年均复合增长率约 4.2%。其中，亚洲将贡献 2025 年至 2030 年全球新增用电量的约 64%，印度、美国和澳大利亚的电力需求增速预测上调幅度最大。

供给方面，大摩预计化石燃料到 2030 年仍将占全球电力结构的约 50%，可靠的煤电和天然气发电有望获得更高的稀缺溢价。同时，2026 年主要市场批发电价同比上涨约 20%，电力行业定价权正从设备制造商向发电运营商转移。

大摩估计，电力需求扩张及电价上涨趋势有望创造约 5000 亿美元价值，并推动相关企业 2028 年每股收益预测上修约 14%，但目前尚未被股票市场充分反映。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/375160

items.content:
Extended公布XTEN代币经济模型：总供应量10亿枚，30%用于社区空投

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，去中心化交易平台 Extended 公布原生代币 XTEN 的代币经济模型，总供应量上限为 10 亿枚，全部于创世时铸造，不设通胀机制。其中，30%（3 亿枚）分配给 Extended Points 计划的符合条件参与者，并将在 TGE 时完全解锁，无需支付费用。

XTEN 主要用于交易手续费折扣、质押奖励及 Vault 收益加成。质押功能将在 TGE 同步上线，用户质押至少 500 枚 XTEN 即可进入相应等级，手续费折扣最高可达 30%，Vault 额外收益加成最高可达 5 倍，单个用户的 Vault 加成存款上限最高为 200 万美元。

代币分配方面，生态基金占 20%（2 亿枚），其中 1.5 亿枚用于质押奖励，5000 万枚用于生态发展；团队、创始人及投资者合计占 50%（5 亿枚），TGE 后前 12 个月不会解锁，此后按照不同归属安排分批释放。

此外，XTEN 总供应量不会增加，交易手续费收入可用于销毁代币，Extended 关联实体也可能通过公开市场回购 XTEN。代币还将原生支持 Circle 的 CCTP，实现 Arc 与其他支持该协议的区块链之间的跨链转移。

Extended 尚未公布 TGE 日期及空投领取窗口。值得注意的是，欧洲经济区（EEA）用户在平台上线初期无法进行 XTEN 现货交易，但仍可领取、持有、质押和转移代币。

items.content:
摩根大通推演中期选举：民主党横扫两院概率为66%，共和党守住两院最利美股

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，摩根大通对美国中期选举后的四种国会权力组合进行了情景分析。其中，民主党同时赢得参众两院控制权的概率最高，达到 66%；共和党守住两院的概率仅为 7%，但对应标普 500 指数在四种情景中最大的预期涨幅。

民主党控制两院（概率 66%）：标普 500 指数可能下跌 0.25%，或上涨 0.5%。市场对更严格 AI 监管、数据中心建设限制的担忧，可能引发 AI 概念股抛售。不过，摩根大通认为，即使限制 AI 产业发展的法案获国会通过，也很难获得足够票数推翻特朗普的总统否决，因此建议交易员考虑在科技股回调时买入。财政赤字支出可能减少，长期美债收益率面临下行压力，部分与特朗普政治捐款有关联的企业高管则可能面临更大的国会调查风险。

民主党控制众议院、共和党控制参议院（概率 26%）：标普 500 指数预计上涨 0.5% 至 1%。市场可能欢迎权力分散带来的立法僵局，因为任何一方都难以单独推动重大政策或扩大政府支出。长期美债收益率可能下降，但部分企业及其领导人仍可能面临国会调查。

共和党守住两院（概率 7%）：标普 500 指数预计上涨 1% 至 1.25%。市场不必立即面对新的国会监管风险，科技企业的额外政策压力也相对有限。不过，财政赤字支出可能进一步增加，推动长期美债收益率走高；特朗普可能继续对伊朗采取军事行动，也是这一情景下的潜在风险。

共和党控制众议院、民主党控制参议院（概率 1%）：标普 500 指数预计上涨 0.25% 至 0.75%。两党分掌国会可能引发更激烈的预算争斗，甚至导致联邦政府停摆。民主党掌握参议院后，仍可开展国会调查，相关企业及人士的调查风险不会消失。

若比特币跌破7.5万美元，主流CEX累计多单清算强度将达10.01亿

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，据 Coinglass 数据，若比特币跌破 7.5 万美元，主流 CEX 累计多单清算强度将达 10.01 亿。

BlockBeats 注：清算图并不是展示精确的待清算的合约数目，或者精确的被清算的合约价值。清算图上的柱子展示的是其实是每个清算簇相对临近清算簇的重要性，即强度。

因此，清算图展现的是标的价格达到某个位置会被影响到什么程度。更高的「清算柱」表示价格到了之后将会因为流动性浪潮产生更加强烈的反应。

items.content:
Anthropic IPO遭投资者压价：估值盼降至1.5万亿，算力承诺近9000亿美元

动察 Beating AI 快讯，随着上周科技股大跌，计划参与 Anthropic IPO 的大型机构投资者开始要求降低估值，希望定在 1.5 万亿至 1.6 万亿美元。投资者担心 AI 投资过热、数据中心建设遭遇阻力，以及巨额算力投入迟迟难以兑现利润。

Anthropic 尚未确定最终估值和发行股数。公司计划最快下周启动路演，争取在 11 月 16 日当周上市。部分投资者希望公司保守定价，为股票上市首日上涨留出空间。

11 月 2 日，Anthropic 还向 SEC 提交了更新版 S-1/A 招股书，披露算力及基础设施合同承诺总额约 8954 亿美元，涵盖云计算采购、数据中心和设备租赁等。其中约 4475 亿美元预计在 2030 年底前发生，剩余大部分延续至 2045 年。仅未来 12 个月，就有约 698 亿美元的合同付款义务。

Anthropic 第三季度营收达到 169.56 亿美元，环比增长约 47%，但第二季度的环比增幅曾高达 144%。营业利润则从第二季度的 9.74 亿美元，转为第三季度亏损 5.67 亿美元。

Anthropic 解释，第三季度有约 50 亿美元算力来自价格更贵的短期合同，另外还计入了约 20 亿美元的非现金员工捐赠匹配费用。新模型降价和客户协议折扣，也抵消了约 6 亿美元的营收增长。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
Binance begins second withdrawal phase, exchange outflows slow
The exchange says additional assets will become available for withdrawal from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday as security checks are completed, following an initial reopening on Sunday.
Binance plans to begin a second phase of cryptocurrency withdrawals on Tuesday, as data shows withdrawal volumes have started to stabilize following last week’s $6.3 billion hack.
Withdrawals for additional assets are scheduled to resume progressively from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday, according to Binance’s latest recovery notice. The rollout follows an initial reopening on Nov. 1.
“Like phase one, reopening will roll out progressively across the assets as security and readiness checks are completed,” said Binance.
The exchange said it was prioritizing tokens based on user demand over the past week. Deposits remain available.
Networks part of the second phase of withdrawals include Binance Smart Chain, Ethereum, Solana, XRP Ledger, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base, according to Binance.
Binance’s list of assets planned for withdrawal. Source: Binance
On Monday, Binance said it also reopened withdrawals for several fiat currencies, including the US dollar, United Arab Emirates dirham, Vietnamese dong, Philippine peso and Indonesian rupiah, adding to a list of 23 other currencies already available for withdrawal.
Binance exchange outflows slow
Data from DefiLlama shows outflows from the crypto exchange have slowed since Sunday, with net outflows on Monday at $2.57 billion, compared to $6.1 billion the day before.
In a separate security reminder, Binance warned that scammers could exploit the phased reopening by impersonating the exchange and offering accelerated withdrawals, sell priority processing, help users claim compensation or direct them to move assets into a purported “Binance vault,” the exchange said.
“Anyone promising to expedite it for a fee is scamming you,” Binance said.
Related: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack

items.content:
HashKey Exchange理财频道上线WisdomTree三只美国国债数字基金，拓展链上固定收益产品布局

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，数字资产金融服务集团 HashKey Group（股票代码：3887.HK）旗下持牌交易平台 HashKey Exchange 宣布，其理财频道已上线 WisdomTree 旗下三只美国国债数字基金 WisdomTree Short-Term Treasury Digital Fund（WTSYX）、WisdomTree 3-7 Year Treasury Digital Fund（WTTSX）及 WisdomTree 7-10 Year Treasury Digital Fund（WTSTX），分别覆盖 1–3 年、3–7 年及 7–10 年美国国债。

三只基金均为 WisdomTree Digital Trust 旗下的美国注册开放式基金，主要投资于美元计价的美国财政部债券，并采用被动式指数投资策略，跟踪对应期限的 Solactive U.S. Treasury Bond Index 表现。产品仅限合资格专业投资者，为投资者提供不同期限的美元计价固定收益投资选择。通过引入不同期限的美国国债数字基金，HashKey Exchange 进一步丰富其链上固定收益类 RWA 产品供给，满足投资者在资产配置、期限管理及风险收益偏好方面的多样化需求。

目前，HashKey Exchange 理财频道已形成覆盖多类资产的 RWA 产品矩阵，包括代币化货币市场基金、贵金属、固定收益、私募信贷及权益类资产等类型（部分产品仅限专业投资者）。此前，HashKey Exchange 已与 WisdomTree 合作上线 SPXUX 和 TECHX 两只代币化美股指数基金，本次新引入 WisdomTree 旗下三只产品，进一步丰富了双方在 RWA 领域的合作布局，也扩充了平台的链上固定收益类 RWA 产品供给，持续提升平台在产品分销与资产服务方面的综合能力，为投资者提供涵盖不同资产类别及期限的多元化投资敞口。

HashKey Exchange 是上市公司 HashKey Holdings Limited (3887.HK) 旗下的数字资产交易平台，致力于在合规丶资金保障、平台安全方面为虚拟资产交易平台定义新标杆，Hash Blockchain Limited（HashKey Exchange）是香港首批持牌零售虚拟资产交易平台。目前已获得香港证券及期货事务监察委员会（证监会）批准，持有在《证券及期货条例》下的第 1 类（证券交易）、第 7 类（提供自动化交易服务），以及在《打击洗钱条例》下的经营虚拟资产交易平台牌照，持牌运营虚拟资产交易平台。HashKey Exchange 已获得 ISO 27001（资讯安全）和 ISO 27701（资料私隐）管理系统认证。为遵守法律法规，HashKey Exchange 不向中国大陆、美国和某些其他司法辖区的用户提供服务。

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
GPT-6开始「手写」神经网络：把游戏规则变成权重，打砖块得分高出20倍

动察 Beating AI 快讯，神经网络里动辄数百万、数亿个参数，过去主要靠训练算法反复调整。MIT 研究团队却发现，GPT-6 Astra 已经能直接分析、修改这些数字，甚至不用训练，就能从零写出一套神经网络。

研究人员把简化版打砖块游戏的规则、源代码和一套权重全为零的神经网络交给 GPT-6，让它自己填写参数。不提供训练数据，也不允许试玩。GPT-6 自己推算球的落点，把预测和移动挡板的逻辑写进网络权重。最终游戏得分达到 517.4，是同等结构、经过 5 亿步强化学习训练的模型的约 20 倍。不过，在另外两款游戏中，它没有超过训练 5 亿步的模型。

研究人员随后让 GPT-6 直接修改阿里 Qwen3.5-0.8B 的权重。它没有重新训练模型，只改动了 0.016% 的参数，就让 MATH-500 数学正确率从 7.9% 升至 48.1%，指令遵循成绩也提高了近 3 倍。

原来，Qwen 经常陷入思考死循环，反复推理却不给出答案。修改前，93% 的数学测试回答会耗尽 32768 个 Token；修改后降至 33.1%。GPT-6 相当于修好了妨碍模型正常答题的毛病。

但换成参数量仅 2.7 亿的 Gemma 3 270M，GPT-6 就没能明显提高数学成绩。这款更小的模型很少陷入死循环，主要问题是算术和推理本身就容易出错，没法靠修改少量权重轻易解决。

研究人员将这种直接读写参数的方法称为「权重空间编程」（Weight-Space Programming）。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/375133

DeepSeek Harness创造者模式：一句话给AI工作台添加新功能

动察 Beating AI 快讯，DeepSeek 展示了 Harness 的 Creator Mode（创造者模式）。Harness 目前提供标准、PTC、极简和创造者四种模式。其中，创造者模式允许用户直接让 AI 开发插件、修改软件界面，再安装到 Harness 中使用，不需要自己编写代码。

比如，想剪辑视频，可以让 AI 做出带时间轴的剪辑工具；想读论文，可以制作支持划线、批注的阅读器；还可以生成海报设计工具、交互式 3D 模型，甚至修改 Harness 的整个界面，换成像素游戏风格。

用户只需描述需求，AI 就会查看 Harness 的开发接口，编写插件代码、完成安装，并检查运行效果。装好的插件可以保留下来，下次打开继续使用。除了新增界面，还能给 Agent 增加工具，让它执行原本不具备的操作。

官方演示中，AI 制作了一个悬浮番茄钟，编写 600 多行前端代码，完成安装和运行，总共耗时 5 分 24 秒。

DeepSeek 还公开了 7 个演示案例的提示词。不过，部分作品经过多轮对话修改，并非输入一句话就能直接得到相同效果。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Felix Ng
items.content:
South Korea urges exchanges to boost cold storage after Binance hack
South Korean crypto exchanges are already required to hold at least 80% of customer crypto in cold wallets, but the regulator is urging more.
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has urged domestic crypto exchanges to increase the proportion of assets held in cold wallets after the $6.3 billion attack on Binance last week.
In a statement Monday, the FSC said it held an emergency meeting with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Financial Security Institute, the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA) and major crypto service providers to review the impact of the Binance hack on South Korea’s crypto market and review exchanges’ security measures.
The FSC said it reviewed exchanges’ IT access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privileges. It also urged providers to increase the proportion of assets held in offline cold wallets.
Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance’s internet-connected hot wallets last week, moving most of the funds in about 20 minutes, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. Binance has said the vast majority of users’ assets are held in cold storage.
South Korean law already requires exchanges to hold at least 80% of users’ crypto assets in cold storage, though cold wallet holdings vary considerably among South Korea’s major exchanges.
At the end of September, Upbit’s cold wallet ratio stood at 99.17%, followed by Bithumb at 94.76% and Coinone at 85%, according to Financial Supervisory Service data cited by local media. Digital X, formerly Korbit, and GOPAX reported ratios of 82.79% and 80.54%, respectively.
Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US
The FSC also urged providers to continuously monitor deposits and withdrawals, secure additional incident response personnel and promptly report and share information about unusual access attempts.
Operators were also asked to set aside additional reserves and implement other security measures that could be introduced immediately to prevent similar breaches. The regulator said it would continue working with relevant agencies and the industry to prevent further attacks and limit potential damage.
Cointelegraph reached out to Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Digital X and GOPAX for comment.
The FSC’s warning comes as the Bank of Korea separately surveys 18 banks and 13 brokerages about their exposure to crypto-related risks, including major exchange hacks and prolonged market downturns. The central bank’s review began before the Binance attack.

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，据 BIT 股票平台数据显示，苹果今晨收盘跌幅 1.83%，盘后再跌 2.5%，为何财报超预期后仍遭市场抛售？今晨苹果发布 2026 财年第四季财报，营收 1144.8 亿美元（同比+11.7%）、EPS 2.10 美元均超预期，iPhone 收入同比大增 17.5% 至约 576 亿美元、Mac 同比增近 24% 表现亮眼。但大中华区收入虽同比增 21% 至约 175 亿美元，仍低于分析师预期约 6.5%；服务业务增速放缓至约 9.8%，为近三年低位，且公司给出的下一季服务收入增速指引仅 8%-9%，明显低于市场预期。
