Explore central Warsaw in voxels - slightly inspired by Minecraft, and MagicaVoxel. You can change the date, time of day and weather, explore the city, or click on a pedestrian to control them (here a bit of inspiration from Dungeon Keeper).

Works best on desktop, but I tried to make it usable on mobile too. The initial load can take a while. It's based on several open datasets, including:

- OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=6/52.02/19.14) - buildings, streets, sidewalks, tram tracks, etc

- GUGiK / Geoportal (https://www.geoportal.gov.pl/) - LiDAR for building heights and trees, aerial imagery for colours

- Warsaw's city tree database (https://mapa.um.warszawa.pl/) - individual tree species, used for seasonal foliage

Open-source (https://github.com/stared/warsaw-vibe-voxel), so feel invited to (re)use it as you wish! --- Top Comments --- [stared]: There are quite a few such other projects, e.g. Streets of Prague ( https://beta.streetsofprague.com/ ), were one can explore Prague in a top-down GTA2-like mode, based on real data. [MisterTea]: Super neat project but I am getting fractional (<1 FPS) frame rates in FF on Linux. Granted, this is an older AMD PC and certainly no power house but it used to run actual Minecraft just fine. [_whiteCaps_]: I really enjoyed visiting Warsaw, I went there for work a few years ago and didn't really know what to expect. If you ever have the chance, I highly recommend the Warsaw Uprising Museum. [radicality]: Nice. At first glance looks cool, but then, oh my, some areas are really butchered :S Poor Old Town and Plac Zamkowy - I'm familiar with the area and at first was scanning trying to find it visually by the features I know are there, but then in this model it's very different (wrong color, many more floors in this model, a 20-story building where at most should be at most a 5-story, the old town castle looking like a gray residential 'blok' and not the prettier structure th... [jesse__]: It's almost unusably slow on my laptop. 3080ti mobile, windows 11, chrome. I opened the profiler and the update appears to be fast enough; roughly hitting 30fps, but there are massive gaps between updates and the actual frame time seems to be about 120ms. Other than that, neat :)

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Bitmine bought another 8,573 ETH, raising holdings to 6,060,506 ETH (about $13.7 billion), or 4.9% of supply—99% of the way to its “Alchemy of 5%” goal.
- Chairman Tom Lee argued the record $6.4 billion Binance hack showed crypto’s resilience, citing six reasons for the muted 4% ETH drop.
- Total holdings hit $14.5 billion; Bitmine remains the top ETH treasury and No. 2 behind Strategy, resumed buying with a $66 million purchase.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak intact, adding 8,573 ETH worth roughly $19 million, while chairman Tom Lee used the record Binance hack to argue that crypto has grown more resilient, not more fragile.
The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings now total 6,060,506 ETH, worth roughly $13.7 billion at a reference price of $2,261 per coin.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
That represents 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, a target it brands the “Alchemy of 5%,” reached in just 15 months. The firm has bought Ethereum every week since launching its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025.
Most of Lee’s commentary focused on last week’s roughly $6.4 billion theft from Binance, which the FBI has attributed to North Korea. Lee called it “a terrible development” but argued the market’s “relatively muted” reaction was “very constructive.” (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)
Lee noted that when North Korea’s Lazarus-linked hackers drained $1.5 billion from Bybit in February 2025, Ethereum fell 8% that day and 20% within a week, whereas ETH slid just 4% after the Binance breach, despite the theft being roughly four times larger.
Lee laid out six reasons for the muted response: Binance’s ability to cover all customer losses, the absence of a cascade of DeFi failures like the one that followed Bybit, swift industry action that cut the potential loss in half, the FBI naming North Korea within two days rather than the months such attributions have taken historically, the fact that the exploit was a “corporate infiltration” of Binance’s infrastructure rather than a blockchain flaw, and the limited price downside itself, which he read as a sign a “crypto bull market is underway.”
Taken together, he said, the episode shows the industry is “increasingly resilient and more capable of absorbing these nation-state assaults.”
Counting cash, other tokens and what it calls “moonshot” investments, Bitmine’s total holdings stood at $14.5 billion as of Nov. 1, including 216 Bitcoin, $498 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and an $82 million position in Eightco Holdings, which it bills as a rare public proxy for indirect OpenAI exposure.
Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, trailing only Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which the release said holds about 848,517 BTC.
Strategy recently resumed its own Bitcoin buying with a $66 million purchase after a brief pause.
Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized staking revenue of roughly $358 million.

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
Fridges in supermarkets across Europe have been hacked and set to defrost for a second time this year as part of a cyberattack that will likely cause millions of euros worth of damage.
BNO News reports that fridges in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, Estonia, and the Netherlands were hacked last night.
Affected fridges were programmed to defrost and reach temperatures up to 158°F (70°C), causing chilled foods to spoil.
Read more: LIVE: Binance resumes withdrawals leading to $6B outflows
Unlike many cybercriminals, the fridge hackers aren’t attempting to extract a crypto ransom or siphon any funds.
Instead, it appears that whoever’s behind the attacks just wants to cause chaos and damage physical infrastructure in Europe.
Someone really doesn’t like functioning fridges
Hundreds of French supermarket fridges were also hacked last month.
At the time, Intermarché CEO Thierry Cotillard told publishers that he expects losses to amount to “tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day.”
Another cyberattack in August also disrupted freezers across at least six US military bases. The Pentagon is now coordinating with French authorities in their investigation.
Potential culprits include teenagers and Russia
Gérôme Billois, who is a partner in the Cybersecurity Business Unit at Wavestone, told The Guardian that the culprits in these attacks will likely be youngsters and activists, or state-sponsored actors.
He suggested that the fridge incident is most likely a destabilisation attack “designed to convey the message to populations that they are not safe, to convey the impression that the government is falling apart, and ultimately to instil fear.”
“Currently there are two international actors known for doing this sort of thing: Iran and Russia,” Billois said.

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Security tokenization can give holders the economic benefits of share ownership without making them shareholders of record.
- Native issuance places the token inside the security's authorized issuance, with a transfer agent maintaining the record.
- Wyoming law recognizes a "certificate token," letting corporate shares be represented on a blockchain.
Most tokenized stocks aren't natively issued on a blockchain. They begin as conventional shares, sit with a broker or custodian, and are then represented by tokens issued separately. In effect, the market has largely replicated traditional securities structures on-chain instead of rethinking them from the ground up. The token "may track the value of the underlying shares," writes Ivan Kan, CMO of tokenization platform T7X, in an essay shared with Decrypt, "but the token holder is not necessarily the shareholder of record."
While the holder owns the price movement, whether they own the share is another matter altogether. The SEC set out three models in January: issuers tokenizing their own shares, third parties issuing tokens against shares held in custody, and firms issuing a separate security for synthetic exposure.
Writing for Forbes' Technology Council in August, Kan cited Pantera Capital research covering 593 tokenized assets across 11 asset classes, of which 77.6% were what Pantera called "digital wrappers around traditional infrastructure" rather than securities in their own right.
"What does the token legally represent, and who authorized it?" Kan asks, setting out an alternative model that T7X Equities is pursuing, which they dub "native issuance." A security exists because an issuer authorizes it, they argue, and "blockchain does not eliminate those corporate and securities-law requirements."
One token, one security, one issuance
Under the native issuance model, the token is part of the authorized issuance from the start, running from issuer authorization to investor verification to transfer-agent validation, aiming at "one security, one authorized issuance, one ownership record, one digital representation."
Wyoming, Delaware, and Nevada corporate law recognizes a "certificate token," allowing shares to be represented electronically on a blockchain. T7X is incorporated in Wyoming and structures its issuances to operate within this framework. The blockchain then becomes "part of the infrastructure supporting the capitalization table" instead of being just another instrument layered on top.
The transfer agent keeps the official master securityholder file and the blockchain records transactions, while the legal record of ownership stays where regulators expect it.
In T7X's administrated offerings, that transfer agent is T7X Equities. Transfer agents register with the SEC and hold the authoritative record of who owns a security, processing transfers and maintaining the master file, which puts the company inside the model it is advocating as well as behind it. Its first example is Tranquil Healthcare Fund I, a Tier 2 Regulation A+ offering of up to $75 million that the SEC qualified on June 29. T7X Equities issues tokens representing its shares on Trusted Smart Chain and delivers them to investors' wallets, the company said.
"There's a registered, SEC-regulated gatekeeper that determines who owns which security at any point in time," T7X Chief Executive Pablo Penaloza said at Consensus in Miami earlier this year. "As long as you have a transfer agent involved, there is no way that securities can disappear without trace."
RWA+
Kan calls the broader category "RWA+." The plus doesn't refer to any single rule, he argues, but the requirement that "compliance and oversight are real," and it rests on three elements. Native issuance creates the token as part of the security's authorized issuance. Integrated compliance writes investor verification and disclosure into the instrument from the start, not as an afterthought. Legally enforceable ownership puts the token holder on the transfer agent's record.
"A receipt is not an asset," Kan wrote in Forbes. "It is a claim wrapped around one, dependent on an intermediary to honor it." Synthetic "PreStocks" tied to SpaceX and Anthropic were never valid claims, he noted, because neither company authorized the transfers. Done properly, he argues, "ownership, compliance and settlement are the same fact."
Whether a token carries the rights of a share is becoming the dividing line elsewhere, too. The SEC's new innovation exemption covers tokenized stocks carrying dividends and voting rights while excluding price-tracking synthetics, and Nasdaq's arrangement with Kraken turns on tokens conveying the same voting rights as ordinary shares.
Penaloza pins the near-term opportunity on companies raising under $100 million, usually between $50 million and $75 million, through Regulation A offerings.
Regulation A+, Kan argues, suits this model because it permits public solicitation and non-accredited participation while requiring audited financials and continuing disclosure. Most tokenized assets rely instead on Regulation D placements, limited to accredited investors. Reg A also opens the door, Penaloza notes, to retirement accounts. Unregistered securities can legally sit in a self-directed IRA, but many brokers won't hold them and most investment advisers steer clients away. "The money is sitting in the older generations' retirement accounts," he said, and a registration attached to the investment is what makes an individual retiree comfortable holding it.
For investors already holding these securities, the benefit is an exit. Shareholders in Reg A and Reg D placements typically receive a paper certificate and then "have to go around and find somebody who will want to give them liquidity," Penaloza said. A native digital security can trade on a secondary market, he said, settling wallet to wallet without a custodian in between.
Giving Reg A and Reg D holdings somewhere to trade would, he argued, "incredibly speed up not only the rate of capital formation, but also the liquidity in the market." Within five years, he predicts, "the total tokenized portfolio will far surpass the existing market capitalization of what is currently trading on all the public markets."

Anthropic修订版IPO招股书：第三季度营收达170亿美元，九个月营收332亿美元，巨额会计亏损仍存

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，人工智能公司 Anthropic（Claude 大模型开发商）今日向 SEC 提交了修订版 IPO 招股说明书（S-1/A）。文件显示，公司商业化进程极为迅猛：2026 年第三季度营收达到 170 亿美元，前九个月合计营收 332.42 亿美元；与此同时，净亏损因可转换票据公允价值变动而飙升至 1040.39 亿美元，但经营层面亏损已大幅收窄。

招股书披露，Anthropic 营收从 2023 年商业化初期的近乎为零，到 2025 年全年约 45.85 亿美元，再到 2026 年前九个月 332 亿美元。其中第三季度单季 170 亿美元，延续了上半年约 163 亿美元的强劲势头。

净收入留存率（NRR）约 900%，显示现有客户支出快速扩张。公司强调其「改进循环」（客户反馈加速模型迭代）与「投资循环」（营收反哺算力与研究）形成正反馈。

经营表现改善明显：前九个月经营亏损收窄至约 12.6 亿美元（主要成本包括算力与基础设施约 188 亿美元、人员约 48.6 亿美元等）。现金及短期投资合计约 1319 亿美元（截至 9 月 30 日），显示融资能力极强。但公司同时披露算力与基础设施相关承诺规模约 8954 亿美元（未来 12 个月到期约 698 亿美元），凸显资本密集与长期锁定风险。

九个月净亏损 1040.39 亿美元中，绝大部分（约 943 亿美元）来自可转换票据、衍生负债等公允价值变动——这是估值上升带来的非现金会计费用，而非实际现金消耗。上半年（截至 6 月 30 日）已录得约 807 亿美元净亏损，修订版延续并更新了这一逻辑。

Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed on November 2 that one of its systems had suffered a cyberattack. The exchange said the incident was quickly contained, customers would not incur losses, and no customer data had been leaked. Deposits and withdrawals have been temporarily suspended as a precaution. Tether said it has frozen more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident.

According to preliminary analysis by blockchain security firm Hypernative, more than $40 million in suspicious transfers were identified across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron. The estimated losses have not been confirmed by the exchange, and the attack method remains unknown. — link

items.content:
Mercado Bitcoin confirms cyberattack, Hypernative estimates over $40M suspected losses

Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed on November 2 that one of its systems had suffered a cyberattack. The exchange said the incident was quickly contained, customers would not incur losses, and no customer data had been leaked. Deposits and withdrawals have been temporarily suspended as a precaution. Tether said it has frozen more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident.

According to preliminary analysis by blockchain security firm Hypernative, more than $40 million in suspicious transfers were identified across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron. The estimated losses have not been confirmed by the exchange, and the attack method remains unknown.

Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin said approximately $38 million in assets were involved in the security incident. Working with Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1, and Chainalysis, the exchange has blocked approximately $11 million and identified additional assets that may be eligible for blocking. Containment efforts remain ongoing. Mercado Bitcoin reiterated that customers will not suffer asset losses and said services will resume once security conditions are fully met, with no timeline announced. — link

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks
Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.
Michael Saylor’s Strategy spent more than three times as much buying back its STRC preferred shares as it did acquiring Bitcoin last week.
Strategy repurchased $208.2 million in STRC and spent about $65.5 million buying 811 Bitcoin (BTC) at an average price of $80,846, according to a Monday 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Strategy sold about 1.18 million MSTR shares for net proceeds of $164 million. About $65.5 million funded its Bitcoin acquisition, while the remaining $98.5 million was allocated to the company’s USD Cash balance, according to the filing. The company held $132.7 million in USD Cash and $4.79 billion in its separate US dollar reserve as of Sunday.
The latest purchases followed about $664 million in STRC buybacks between Oct. 1 and Oct. 25, compared with about $72 million in Bitcoin acquisitions over that period.
Strategy’s STRC preferred stock rose 0.1% in pre-market trading on Monday, to $99.22, or about 0.8% below its $100 target price, according to Yahoo Finance. Strategy’s policy is not to issue new STRC shares below $100, limiting that source of funding while the stock trades below its target.
Another Bitcoin treasury company, Japan’s Metaplanet, reported buybacks of its common shares on Monday. It spent about 25.27 billion yen ($160 million) to buy back 96.45 million shares between Oct. 14 and Saturday, representing roughly 7.1% of its issued shares.
Related: CryptoQuant CEO calls rising Bitcoin hashrate ‘indirect bullish signal’ from institutions
items.title: Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Tom Lee分析Binance被盗：金额巨大但跌幅有限，为牛市信号

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，Bitmine 董事长 Thomas「Tom」Lee 在最新公告中表示：「上周晚些时候，Binance 遭到黑客攻击，价值 63 亿美元的客户资金被盗。根据 Binance 和其他媒体的报道，此次漏洞源于承包商渗透了 Binance 的企业基础设施。FBI 已指名朝鲜为肇事者。尽管这是一个可怕的进展，但在我看来，加密市场相对温和的反应是非常具有建设性的，特别是与此前大规模加密盗窃案的市场反应相比。」

「2025 年 2 月，Bybit 同样遭到朝鲜黑客攻击（作案手法完全不同），15 亿美元的客户加密资产被盗。Bybit 盗窃案宣布当天，ETH 下跌了 8%，一周内下跌了 20%。相比之下，自 Binance 盗窃案披露以来，ETH 仅下跌了 4%。我们认为，尽管此次盗窃案的规模约为上次的四倍，但市场的反应却要温和得多。」Lee 继续说道。

Bitmine 认为，有 6 个原因解释了为何 Binance 盗窃案的市场反应较为温和。分别是：

· Binance 有足够的财务能力来承担所有客户损失。· 没有出现 Bybit 盗窃案后那种 DeFi 协议连环崩溃的情况。

· 行业的迅速行动将潜在损失减少了 50%。

· FBI 在盗窃案发生 2 天内就点名朝鲜（DPRK）为责任方。而历史上，当局在以往的盗窃案中最多需要 180 天才能指认 DPRK。

· 该漏洞是对 Binance 基础设施的「企业渗透」，而非区块链本身的漏洞。

· 有限的价格下行空间是加密「牛市」正在进行的信号，尽管近期价格有所下跌。

Tom Lee 表示，综合来看，Bitmine 认为这表明加密行业正变得越来越有韧性，也更有能力吸收这些针对金融基础设施的国家级攻击。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/375060

--- From telegram ---
Elliptic：朝鲜黑客正洗白Binance被盗超32亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，据区块链分析公司 Elliptic 披露，朝鲜相关黑客在盗取交易平台 Binance 约 64.3 亿美元加密资产后，正以高度自动化方式进行复杂洗钱。截至文章更新时，相关资金在不到四天内已使用约 1.2 万个钱包、横跨 11 条区块链，发起逾 4 万笔交易，平均约每 25 秒新建一个钱包。

Elliptic 称，目前仍有约 32.4 亿美元留在与盗窃相关的地址中，主要为 ETH 与 BTC；另有约 28.5 亿美元已被冻结或扣押，可确认变现离场的金额可忽略不计。洗钱路径以波场（Tron）为主，资金被拆分至约 7700 个地址并跨链桥接至以太坊，至少约 1.47 亿美元已从波场桥出。自 11 月 1 日起，部分 ETH、SOL、NEAR、XRP 开始转移；约 28 枚 BTC（约合 220 万美元）首次进入 Wasabi 风格的 coinjoin 混币。Elliptic 认为，操作呈现固定节奏与批量特征，指向常规自动化程序而非 AI 自主决策，并预计攻击者后续将参照 Bybit 案路径，把 ETH 分批换成比特币，再经场外经纪商等渠道变现。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/375036

--- From telegram ---
Arkham：Binance黑客向平台充值地址存入400万美元，或涉嵌套服务

BlockBeats 注：Arkham 指出的「嵌套服务」是一种通过借用大型合规交易平台（如 Binance）的账户来为第三方客户提供服务的中间商。可以将其理解为一种「寄生」在大型交易平台上的二级服务商。

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 3 日，据彭博社报道，在 Binance 遭遇创纪录的 63 亿美元黑客攻击后，其提高了向部分在其平台上交易的做市商提供的激励，以提振其平台上的交易活动。

据知情人士透露，在上周发生安全漏洞后不久，该公司就联系了规模较小的交易公司，在现货和期货市场提供更高的返佣。

根据其网站信息，Binance 主要根据做市商提供的流动性将其分为不同级别。提供更大交易量份额的公司有资格获得更高的级别，通常会获得更大的返佣，从而降低其交易成本。

知情人士表示，在这项为期一周的促销活动中，所谓的 2 级和 3 级做市商将获得与 4 级参与者（该平台最高级别的群体）相同的返佣率。知情人士补充道，这些变化旨在为规模较小的流动性提供商提供更高的财务激励，使其在该交易平台报价并维持更深的订单簿。

Binance 的一位发言人表示，Binance 在安全漏洞事件后的最新举措有助于安抚市场，并补充说：「正如我们优先考虑清晰的沟通一样，我们立即采取措施来维持我们的核心优势：流动性。」

做市商通过持续提供买卖报价发挥着核心作用，其提供的流动性使其他投资者能够进行交易，而不会导致价格出现剧烈波动。根据 Talos 的数据，黑客攻击后的 24 小时内，Binance 上的比特币订单簿深度下降了约 30%，价格 1% 范围内的深度从 4500 万美元降至 3200 万美元。市场深度是衡量在不引起价格剧烈波动的情况下能够吸收多少交易的指标。

items.content:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors chop over weekend in Binance hack aftermath; BTC at $77.6k
- Binance turns on withdrawals post-hack, sees $3.64B exodus
- FBI and Secret Service open probes into Binance hack
- BTC ETFs lose $643M in outflows on Friday, flip October to red
- Nvidia and Micron added to list of companies objecting to tokenized shares on OKXICE, now at 50
💸 The Binance Hack Just Cost Bitcoin ETFs Their Whole Month
Through Thursday, October was a quiet, slightly positive month for Bitcoin ETFs. Then North Korea took $6.4 billion out of Binance five minutes after the closing bell, and Friday’s single session erased the entire month.
To recap the Binance hack, attackers drained roughly $6.4 billion from Binance’s hot wallets across about 10 blockchains, with most of it inside 20 minutes on Thursday afternoon. That’s more than four times the old record, the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025. Both firms attribute it to TraderTraitor, the North Korea-linked group that also hit Bybit.
The entry point has changed since Friday. Binance first blamed a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, then found “additional points of breach.” On Ethereum, the attacker used 50 pre-signed authorizations to turn a Binance hot wallet into a contract that emptied itself—a failure of Binance’s own signing approvals, not of Ethereum. No private keys leaked. The attacker wiped its tooling on the way out.
Friday was the aftermath, and it was bloody. Bitcoin ETFs bled $643.3 million on Friday, the biggest day of the month, ending a four-session buying streak. That one day took October from +$127 million to −$515.9 million. September was +$2.65 billion. The ETH ETFs were worse: −$1.61 billion for October, their worst month since launch, and an 11-session losing streak into the weekend.
Now the biggest players in the U.S. government are reacting. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig told CNBC the hack “proves our exact point.” “The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards.” He’s pitching a “federal option”—let offshore venues register with the CFTC and meet US cybersecurity standards. He also notes the hole came in “from someone’s laptop,” not from a blockchain. The FBI and Secret Service have also both opened probes.
Binance CEO Richard Teng says the company covers every dollar from corporate funds and SAFU, with $6.34 billion already set aside. CZ: “It hurts, but we survive.” Withdrawals were turned back on over the weekend and over $3.6B has exited so far according to QCP.
So what to watch from here? Monday’s inflows (or outflows) will be telling. If Friday’s bleeding continues to Monday, it’s a signal that the pain might just be beginning. Also, watch Binance. They have to buy roughly $1.3 billion of BTC, ETH, and BNB on the open market and OTC to top off the reimbursement pool—a forced bid underneath a market that just got hit. And then there’s Selig and the FBI; be on the lookout from updates from those agencies as the Binance hack aftermath carries forward.
🌎 Macro Crypto and Markets
- Crypto majors are mixed in the Binance hack aftermath; BTC -0.3% at $77.6k; ETH +1% at $2,280; SOL -1% at $94; HYPE -3% at $86; ZEC even at $1,245
- No notable alt movers
- Oil -4% at $99; Gold +0.3% at $3,910
- Stock futures are green as oil falls, tech rebounds; DOW +0.35%, Nasdaq +0.7%
- The FBI and Secret Service opened probes into the $6.4 billion Binance hack, with the bureau confirming it is “working with public and private partners to assess its scope and coordinate investigative steps”
- Binance set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets, about $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens that were taken; QCP reports $3.64B of net outflows since Binance reopened withdrawals
- CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said the hack “proves our exact point” about the crypto market rules his agency proposed earlier this month
- Elon Musk trolled Binance with a grimacing emoji on a post estimating $1 billion in losses, prompting CZ to reply “Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop” and to point out that Binance’s SpaceX shares—acquired through its $500 million stake in the Twitter takeover—are now “worth more than a billion”
- Issuer objections to tokenized share trading on OKXICE reached 50 companies, with Nvidia, Micron, Nike, Costco and Reddit among the latest to opt out; leaves just 12 of the 62 names the OKX-ICE joint venture originally planned to list
Corporate Treasuries & ETFs
- The Bitcoin ETFs saw $643M in net outflows on Friday, flipping the month of October from +$127M to -$516M net; the ETH ETFs saw $156M in outflows and $1.61B in outflows on the month
Meme Coin Tracker
- Meme leaders were slightly red; DOGE -1%, SHIB -2%, PEPE -2%, PENGU -3%, TRUMP +2%, SPX +1%, BONK -3%
- Robinhood chain leaders were mixed; Pons -4% to $155M; Cashcat +7% at $100M; AI -5% at $62M; Orbio +20% and WTH +15% led top movers
- Solana top movers included Anakin +120%, Gato +50%, and Choo +90%; Stonk -7% to $92M
💰 Token, Airdrop & Protocol Tracker
- Pump.fun led onchain protocols in revenue on the day with $1.42M, followed by Hyperliquid at $1.23M and Collector Crypt at $315k
- Crypto card issuer KAST said it will end Points earning on November 30 and replace the program with KAST Pioneer Units, a new loyalty credit for early users
🚚 What is happening in NFTs?
- NFT leaders were mixed; Punks +2% at 30.4 ETH, BAYC -5% at 5.92 ETH, Pudgy -5% at 2.37 ETH
- Quotrons (+15%) and Argonauts (+13%) led top movers
- ACK changed the art on Argonauts to max pain v3; unclear what happens next

items.content:
I was reminded today of AI Adoption Rate Trending Down for Large Companies, a chart produced by Apollo Global Management in September 2025, which appeared to show a slowdown in U.S. corporate AI adoption based on numbers collected by the U.S. Census Bureau. At the time I used that chart to demonstrate GPT-5 data analysis, and then to experiment with Claude's new Code Interpreter. I decided to try running those numbers again to see what had changed over the past year, and in doing so learned that the Bureau has fallen foul of Executive Order 14434, aka the asinine Super Intelligence one.

First, the updated chart

Every two weeks the U.S. Census Bureau runs a survey called the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (aka BTOS). Each time it goes to 200,000 businesses out of 1.2 million total - the surveyed group (a "panel") cycles such that an individual business only completes the survey every twelve weeks.

The latest data is published on alternating Thursdays at 10am.

I used the most recent numbers (published October 22, 2026) to create a new version (GPT-6 Astra Extra High transcript) of the AI adoption chart, updated to reflect both the last twelve months and a change that was made to the survey question sent out by the Bureau:

Here's a link to the larger image.

For comparison, here's that AI adoption chart from last year (my GPT-5 version):

In September 2025 the largest (250+ employees) companies answered "yes" around 12% of the time to the question about whether they used AI in "producing goods or services".

Under the new "any business function" wording, by February 2026, those same large companies answered "yes" around 30% of the time, and by October 2026 that had increased to around 40%.

The data in the above chart comes from the "Employment size class" XLSX file, available from here. Here's a copy of the file I used.

You can view the survey document that is sent out to businesses - here's my snapshot copy of that 346KB PDF.

The changing language of the questions

As the chart demonstrates, the question asked by the Bureau changed in a material way on November 17th, 2025. Prior to that date, the question they asked was this (emphasis mine):

In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in producing goods or services? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)

On December 3rd, 2025, the Bureau announced a significant change to that question. Here's the replacement:

In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)

No more "producing goods or services" - now it's "in any of its business functions"! This means that the answers to the question before and after November 17th are not directly comparable.

From October 19, 2026, they ask about Super Intelligence

When I went looking for the updated question language in the latest XLSX file, I couldn't find it. I found this instead:

In the last two weeks, did this business use Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of SI use include: SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service; SI-powered forecasting or pricing; SI-driven computer vision for quality control, etc.)

The BTOS about page explains what happened:

Beginning with the October 19, 2026 collection, instrument wording was updated due to Executive Order 14434.

The current numbers reflect the old Artificial Intelligence survey wording - the first survey results reflecting the Super Intelligence wording are due for publication on Thursday.

Is this going to affect the survey?

The obvious open question here is whether this wording change is going to affect the survey results.

The businesses answering this survey will have last seen that question twelve weeks ago, when it was still called AI. Hopefully the new language isn't going to confuse them, especially since the survey helpfully spells out "formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI".

I can't help but laugh at the absurdity of "SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service" though.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Andrew Fenton
items.content:
AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.
The world is headed towards a future in which AI agents will trade stocks and crypto, shop for your family, and much more. But what happens when a bot misinterprets an instruction to buy $10K of “blue chip stocks” and instead buys $10K of Bluebird-brand frozen chips?
Low-level agent disputes like this aren’t suited to the expensive and time-consuming existing legal system. Enter Internet Court, a new protocol that enables agents and humans to enter into contracts, with funds kept in escrow until the terms are judged to have been met.
The dispute resolution mechanism baked into the process employs GenLayer, an open, delegated proof-of-stake network of validators hooked up to AI models.
Operating in beta for the past year, it currently processes around 12,000 decisions per day. It authenticates user-uploaded photos for Collective Memory and resolves arguments on argue.fun. Mainnet is expected to launch next month.
The concept is a modern spin on the famous jury theorem proposed by philosopher Nicolas de Condorcet who argued the probability of reaching the correct answers increases as the number of independent evaluators grows.
For Internet Court that means setting up a jury of AI agents from various models in the Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek families, along with a range of others.
“It’s not making the decision by using a single AI that would have some biases,” explains co-founder and CEO of GenLayer Albert Castellana. “It’s actually using a lot of different AIs, up to 1,500 different AIs. And when that happens, you have essentially better responses.”
“One is left-leaning, the other one is right-leaning. That’s how you get a better answer because one cancels the other.”
OK, but how does it actually work?
Disputes are resolved by sending the details to a randomly selected jury of five GenLayer validators, all running a different AI model. An initial decision is reached within minutes and is based on a simple majority vote, but the decision can be appealed to a wider jury of 11 agents, and then 23, and more and more until you hit the system’s limit.
Castellana says finality typically occurs within 30 minutes. “If you wait until maximum finality, it is escalating rounds of appeal. You start with five, and it escalates to fifteen hundred, which could be three hours.” 
The Court has 35 members in its open consortium so far, including well-known crypto firms such as ZKsync, NEAR, Consensys and UMA — which resolves disputes for Polymarket.
Source: Internet Court
GenLayer has been in development for almost four years, and began life as an attempt to come up with a better way to evaluate what information is worthy of inclusion in an online knowledge base like Wikipedia.
In theory, anyone is supposed to be able to correct mistakes in the online encyclopedia but in practice, controversial topics from crypto to the war in Gaza get locked, with a small group of powerful editors getting the final say on contested information.
“The original idea behind GenLayer came with […] how could we have a decentralized Wikipedia?” he explains.
Related: Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins — CFTC chair
Intelligent contracts, not smart contracts
GenLayer enables a new form of smart contract dubbed an “intelligent contract” that allows for subjective judgment. For example, you could contract a freelance writer and allow the system to automatically judge if their content is any good before paying them.
“We have a platform doing exactly this — paying influencers to write content online and then getting the money out,” he explains.
“Intelligent contracts can do code. They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says.
The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract.
Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. 
But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment.
The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety.
Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims.
GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer
AI to judge prediction markets?
A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly.  In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.”
Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably.
”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.”
Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans.
”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.”
Source: Derek Guy
Does AI have good judgment?
Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments.
Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction.
A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink.
Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.”

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof
Binance’s SAFU Bitcoin wallet now holds about 7,500 BTC after a 7,499 BTC transfer linked to the hack, with no timeline for restoring the $1 billion fund.
Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack.
The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).
As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer.
The theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history, forced Binance to suspend withdrawals while it worked to replace the stolen assets. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea on Saturday, identifying the hackers as TraderTraitor.
Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions.
The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses.
SAFU policy sets no deadline to replace funds used after hacks
Binance’s SAFU policy outlines regular monitoring and rebalancing of the fund’s market value.
“If the fund’s market value falls below US $800 million due to BTC price fluctuations, Binance will rebalance the fund to restore its value to $1 billion,” it states.
Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
The policy does not specify a timeline for replenishing funds withdrawn following a security incident.
Binance did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s questions about SAFU’s remaining reserves, further deployments and plans to replenish the fund.
Binance releases verification proof for post-hack reserves
Binance said Monday that users could now verify their balances against its Saturday proof-of-reserves snapshot after it completed the accompanying cryptographic proof.
The exchange said the snapshot showed customer holdings in 10 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, were backed at least 1:1.
The exchange plans to take another snapshot covering more tokens on Wednesday, with the accompanying proof expected to take another 40 to 50 hours to generate.

In brief
- Strategy bought 811 BTC for $65.5 million between October 26 and November 1, resuming purchases after skipping a week, according to an SEC filing.
- The company also spent $208.2 million of its USD Cash buying back STRC, leaving that balance at $132.7 million, down from $242.4 million a week earlier.
- Strategy now holds 849,327 BTC, acquired for $64.08 billion at an average of about $75,451 per coin.
Strategy bought 811 BTC for $65.5 million last week, the company said on Monday, resuming its Bitcoin purchases after a one-week pause.
The Bitcoin treasury firm paid an average of $80,846 per coin between October 26 and November 1, funding the purchases by selling 1,178,552 shares of MSTR stock for $164 million in net proceeds, according to an SEC filing. Of that, $65.5 million went to Bitcoin and $98.5 million to its USD Cash account.
Strategy has acquired 811 $BTC and repurchased $208M of $STRC. As of 11/1/26, we hold 849,327 BTC and $4.9B of USD Assets. $MSTRhttps://t.co/fk7kWJxf3L
— Strategy (@Strategy) November 2, 2026
Strategy now holds 849,327 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.08 billion at an average of about $75,451 per coin.
The company also bought back 2,092,035 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock, for $208.2 million, all paid from USD Cash. That is up from $204.9 million the previous week, when Strategy paused its Bitcoin buying for the first time since mid-September. The week before that, it bought 267 BTC for $22.1 million.
USD Cash, the pool Strategy keeps for general purposes including buying Bitcoin, fell to $132.7 million from $242.4 million a week earlier. Its separate USD Reserve, which covers preferred dividends and interest on its debt, stood at $4.79 billion after paying out $43.4 million in dividends. About $748.6 million remains available under its program for repurchasing preferred stock.
Strategy put its combined USD assets at $4.9 billion and its "USD Duration," its measure of how long those assets could cover dividends and interest, at 3.3 years, it tweeted.
STRC's daily dividends begin
The purchases come as STRC moves to a new dividend schedule. Shareholders approved daily dividends on Strategy's four preferred stocks last week, with STRC's first daily record date falling on November 1.
Mizuho Financial Group maintained its Outperform rating and $165 price target on MSTR following Strategy's third-quarter earnings call, pointing to a stronger balance sheet with net leverage down to 2.4% from 8.4%, according to a summary of the note. But analyst Dan Dolev also flagged dilution concerns, noting that Bitcoin per share has fallen 3.7% this year.
Strategy also faces possible removal from MSCI's equity indexes under a rule the index provider finalized in October, which treats companies dominated by a single asset as ineligible. MSCI will publish the list of affected companies on November 11.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is launching a targeted review of jurisdictions with significant crypto activity to address gaps in how governments apply global anti-money laundering standards.
On Friday, the FATF, an intergovernmental body that sets global standards to combat money laundering, announced that the review would focus primarily on jurisdictions with “materially important” virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity, taking their existing assessment status into account.
The watchdog said its regular assessments and follow-up procedures would remain the main tools for evaluating compliance.
Initial findings will be published in June 2027, with further results in October 2027. The review will also be followed by monitoring and faster reporting to track progress in addressing deficiencies.
The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication.
The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted.
The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas.
The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers.
Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases
items.title: FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.
The hackers behind Binance’s $6.3 billion theft have begun converting stolen Solana tokens into Bitcoin after largely emptying the wallets used to launder funds on Tron, according to blockchain investigators.
Lookonchain reported Sunday that the hackers had moved 486,970 Solana (SOL) tokens, worth about $46.4 million, and were swapping them for Bitcoin (BTC) through Relay.
The activity involves funds that escaped the freezes imposed after Thursday’s theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history. Industry partners, including Tether and Circle, froze about $3 billion in stolen assets, while investigator SomaXBT estimated the attackers still controlled about $3.5 billion.
Binance said the attack compromised its hot wallets, with early findings pointing to a hacked employee laptop before investigators identified additional breach points. The exchange began restoring withdrawals Sunday, pledged to cover the losses and has been working with US authorities to trace and recover the stolen assets.
Related: OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B
Chainalysis said Sunday that most of the hackers’ temporary holding wallets on Tron had been emptied as laundering activity expanded to Solana. It put the value of the Tron transfers at about $500 million.
The $500 million figure counted transfers during laundering, including repeated movements between wallets, SomaXBT said in response. About $242 million actually left the Tron holding wallets, he said.
Chainalysis said Friday that hackers may be using automation to obscure the trail, citing thousands of transactions in a short period. The firm observed funds circulating repeatedly between wallets, sometimes returning to addresses used earlier in the sequence.
Source: Chainalysis
FBI asks crypto services to block hackers’ transactions
Some stolen funds also reached centralized exchange Gate. Lookonchain reported Monday that the hackers had deposited about $250,000 there over the preceding 12 hours.
Gate subsequently said it had frozen two linked accounts and would cooperate with law enforcement. Its statement did not specify how much money was frozen.
The FBI on Saturday attributed Thursday’s theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hackers and published wallet addresses linked to the stolen assets.
The agency, US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation urged THORChain node operators, exchanges and decentralized finance (DeFi) services to block transactions involving those addresses or funds traced back to them.
Investigators had observed the hackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ether (ETH) and expected further laundering through DeFi and instant swap services, the FBI said.
Magazine: THORChain founder rejects freeze request, CZ thanks Secret Service: Hodler’s Digest
items.title: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- BTCPay Server urged operators to shut down their instances on Sunday after reports that attackers were sweeping hot wallets on servers running the software.
- The project later said the attack targeted versions 2.4.1 or older, and that it had no credible reports of drains among users running the latest 2.4.7 release.
- BTCPay released 2.4.7 on Thursday as an emergency update fixing one critical and several medium-severity vulnerabilities found by Anthropic's scanner.
BTCPay Server, a free, open-source tool businesses use to accept Bitcoin payments, told operators to switch off their servers on Sunday after reports that attackers were draining the hot wallets connected to them.
"We are receiving reports of hot wallets on BTCPay Servers being swept by unauthorized attackers," the project tweeted at 5:25 p.m. ET. "If you're running an instance, please shut it down (./btcpay-down.sh) until we complete the investigation."
🚨 We are receiving reports of hot wallets on BTCPay Servers being swept by unauthorized attackers.
If you're running an instance, please shut it down (./btcpay-down.sh) until we complete the investigation.
— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 1, 2026
About two hours later, BTCPay founder Nicolas Dorier said the reports appeared to involve releases older than version 2.4.2, and that the attacker had logged in to affected servers with administrator access.
Later on Sunday, the project said its investigation had identified an attack vector targeting instances running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. "We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release," it said, urging everyone to keep their software updated and asking affected users to send details and logs to its security team.
Some hosting providers, including LunaNode, have shut down BTCPay instances automatically to stop older versions from being exploited, the project said. BTCPay has not said how many servers were affected or how much Bitcoin was taken.
Hot wallets and BTCPay's emergency update
Because BTCPay is self-hosted, each merchant runs the software on their own server, and there is no central operator that can switch instances off. Merchants can choose to run a hot wallet, which stores the wallet's seed on that internet-connected server so it can sign transactions automatically. BTCPay's own documentation labels the feature "DANGER" and warns that it "comes with security implications."
The attacks come days after BTCPay released version 2.4.7 on Thursday as an emergency update fixing one critical and several medium-severity vulnerabilities, which it said were brought to its attention through Anthropic's frontier open-source software scanner. BTCPay has not said whether the attacks exploited any of those flaws.
It is not the first security scare for the project this year. In August, BTCPay warned that a critical vulnerability in all versions before 2.4.2 was being actively exploited, and told users to update or shut down their servers. Supporters of the project later funded a recovery bounty of 10% of any stolen funds returned, capped at 3 BTC.

香港金管局推出SAGE项目，成立代理式金融专家小组

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，据香港金融管理局公告，金管局今日宣布推出 SAGE 项目，全称为 Securing Agentic Finance with Governance and Enablement，意即「结合管治与赋能，构建安全可靠的代理式金融」，旨在推动代理式金融在香港的负责任发展及应用，并同步成立代理式金融专家小组汇聚业界意见。

金管局指出，随着代理式人工智能技术日趋成熟，金融业在推进内部采用的同时，正进一步探索人工智能代理如何使金融服务更有效率和安全。SAGE 项目将聚焦四个主要范畴：一是市场发展及应用场景探索，支持市场参与者验证解决方案，潜在方向包括企业对消费者（B2C）的代理式购物及日常支付、企业对企业（B2B）的采购及财资管理，以及机器对机器（M2M）按用量支付数字服务费用；二是代理身分，探讨核实人工智能代理身分及获授权限的方法，包括「认识你的代理（KYA）」措施及身分认证机制；三是互通性标准，促进业界就相关标准及协议的讨论，以支持生态内安全畅顺互动；四是法律及监管框架，就管治安排、法律责任及消费者保障等议题交流意见。

为汇聚专业知识和观点，金管局成立代理式金融专家小组支持 SAGE 项目，成员包括金融机构、科技服务提供商、专业服务机构及学术界等持份者。金管局总裁余伟文表示，代理式金融具重塑金融服务提供和使用方式的潜力，希望透过一系列措施并促进与业界专家交流，在推动创新的同时巩固香港在下一代金融科技领域的领先地位，确保代理式金融符合用户最佳利益并维持金融体系稳定。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
From Uptober to Hacktober: Are Bitcoin’s seasonal patterns becoming obsolete?
Bitcoin lost 7.3% in October 2026 after another decline the previous year, despite the month’s historically strong returns, as analysts reassess seasonal signals.
Bitcoin’s back-to-back October losses have put its “Uptober” reputation under the microscope as analysts weigh seasonal trends against institutional demand and economic conditions.
Bitcoin fell 7.3% in October 2026, following a roughly 4% decline a year earlier, according to CoinGlass data.
The losses defied October’s historically bullish reputation, which earned it the nickname “Uptober.” This year, industry figures turned to darker labels, including “Black October” and “Hacktober,” amid a wave of crypto security incidents, including Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack.
Bitcoin’s seasonal trends shift as monthly volatility declines
October has historically delivered Bitcoin’s highest median return at 15.4%, with gains in 10 of 13 years through 2025, according to Andrew Yang, a researcher at crypto analytics firm Kaiko.
September’s historically bearish reputation has weakened as well. Bitcoin has posted gains every September since 2023, which could reflect traders buying ahead of an expected October rally, Yang told Cointelegraph.
Bitcoin’s narrowing price swings may also be making seasonal trends less pronounced, Yang said. Its typical monthly move has declined from 14% between 2013 and 2016 to 9.6% since 2024, leaving less room for sharp seasonal rallies, he added.
Are institutions rewriting Bitcoin’s calendar?
Analysts also pointed to institutional investment and broader economic conditions as increasingly important influences on Bitcoin’s price.
Justin d’Anethan, head of research at Arctic Digital, pointed to exchange-traded fund (ETF) flows and corporate Bitcoin buyers, saying their investment decisions are shaped more by liquidity, interest rates and investment mandates than seasonal trading narratives.
Related: Bitcoin ETF flows give mixed read on institutional demand: CoinShares
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $515 million in net outflows in October, while spot Ether ETFs saw a record $1.61 billion in monthly withdrawals.
Yang cautioned that spot Bitcoin ETFs, approved in January 2024, are too recent to assess. Still, Bitcoin “increasingly trades like a macro asset, driven more by economic data and institutional flows than by the calendar,” he said.
Two October losses don’t settle the question
Despite two consecutive October losses, analysts cautioned against writing off Uptober entirely.
Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said October has generally performed better during Bitcoin bull markets and worse during bear markets, making the broader market cycle an important factor when comparing returns.
“Price performance depends more on spot demand dynamics than cyclical patterns, and demand doesn’t care about the calendar,” Moreno told Cointelegraph.
Related: Bitcoin risks worst October in 12 years as tech sell-off spreads to gold
Markus Levin, co-founder of XYO, said that traders may be anticipating seasonal gains earlier. “When enough people expect a rally in October, the rally gets priced in before the month arrives,” he said.
“Uptober has historical validity but, like other seasonality metrics, it can also fail at times,” said Arctic Digital’s d’Anethan.
Magazine: Cybersecurity’s Black October: How to protect yourself

腾讯Hyra 2.0迈向AI自主科研：从头训练模型、设计机器人，甚至参与研发下一代AI

动察 Beating AI 快讯，腾讯混元发布科研 Agent Hyra 2.0，将研究重点从针对单个难题反复试错，扩展到研发能够长期复用的科学模型、算法和工具。

为了让 AI 持续开展数天甚至数周的研究，Hyra 2.0 将工作分给 Overall、Mission、Worker 三层 Agent，分别负责资源协调、研究规划和实验执行。任务会持久化保存，等待训练结果时也能推进其他研究。每项结论需要附上代码、日志等证据，必要时交给独立 Agent 复核。有效经验还会沉淀成 Skill，供后续任务使用。

腾讯披露，Hyra 2.0 已经从头训练出两款蛋白质模型。其中，196 万参数的 HyInv 能根据目标骨架设计蛋白质序列，生成速度比常用的 ProteinMPNN 快 57 倍。在单张 H20 GPU 的预热测试中，生成 128 条约 400 个残基的序列只需约 50 毫秒。另一款 HyPLM-Flash 有 6.5 亿参数，使用了 7260 亿训练 token。两款模型的权重、推理代码和技术报告均已公开。

Hyra 2.0 还参与优化开源 RISC-V 处理器「香山」，使 SPEC CPU2006 每 GHz 性能提高 5.79%，芯片面积仅增加 0.3%。

它还设计了一只五根手指长短递增的「旋梯手」。这只手最初比原有最优设计慢约 11%，但经过相同预算的控制算法训练后，仿真旋转速度反而快了 28.6%。

目前，Hyra 2.0 也已参与下一代混元模型的预训练、后训练及推理系统优化，尝试让 AI 通过改进研发工具，帮助训练出更强的下一代 AI。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Trezor lifts password ceiling after Coldcard’s $100M wallet thefts
Trezor cited July’s Coldcard attacks, in which strong passphrases helped protect some users whose wallet recovery information was compromised.
Hardware wallet maker Trezor has increased the maximum length of optional wallet passphrases from 50 to 128 characters.
On Sunday, Trezor said the change is available in its Trezor Suite with updated device firmware. Older firmware still limits passphrases to 50 characters.
According to Trezor, a passphrase acts like an additional password that users set alongside their wallet’s recovery phrase. An attacker who obtains the recovery phrase would still need the correct passphrase to access funds in that wallet.
Trezor cited the Coldcard attacks in July, when a firmware flaw caused some devices to generate recovery phrases with insufficient randomness, allowing attackers to reconstruct them. Trezor said strong, unique passphrases protected some affected users.
The update follows a separate warning involving Trezor’s own devices.
On Friday, the company advised customers who bought wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds to new wallets.
An Indonesian customer reported a suspected implant inside a Trezor Safe 5 that could capture on-screen information, including recovery phrases, and transmit it over a cellular network. Trezor said Friday it had not examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.
Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack
items.title: Trezor lifts password ceiling after Coldcard’s $100M wallet thefts

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- The FBI said North Korea's TraderTraitor was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, and published hundreds of addresses linked to the hack.
- Binance began restoring withdrawals on Sunday, processing $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits in the first nine and a half hours.
- The exchange said the net outflow represented 2.1% of its $171 billion in assets, and it has since reopened fiat withdrawals, including U.S. dollars.
The FBI has confirmed that North Korea was behind last week's theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, as the exchange began reopening withdrawals and reported billions of dollars leaving the platform.
In an alert published on Saturday, the FBI said the attack was carried out by North Korean hackers it refers to as "TraderTraitor," confirming the attribution blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis made on Friday.
The FBI is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, on or about October 29, 2026. The FBI refers to this specific North… pic.twitter.com/TBUvUFln4n
— FBI Cyber Branch (@FBICyberBranch) October 31, 2026
The FBI, together with the Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, has seen the hackers converting stolen assets mainly into Ethereum, and expects them to launder the funds further through DeFi and instant swap services, the bureau said. It urged node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other crypto businesses to block transactions involving hundreds of Ethereum addresses, 19 Bitcoin addresses and one Solana address it linked to the theft.
The Secret Service, which is also investigating the theft, said on Sunday that its investigators worked with industry partners to identify and freeze "a significant portion" of the stolen crypto within minutes of the attack. That work continues with the FBI, IRS Criminal Investigation, the U.S. Attorney's Offices for Washington, D.C. and the Central District of California, and the Justice Department's computer crime and national security divisions, the agency said.
The laundering is already well underway. After the attack, the hackers moved more than $500 million on Tron through more than 1,000 addresses, over 3,000 deposits and several Tron-based DeFi protocols, blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said on Sunday. Most of those staging wallets have now been drained, with funds leaving Tron through cross-chain services including Chainflip, Relay, THORChain and NEAR for dozens of fresh wallets on Ethereum, Bitcoin and other chains, and the launderers have started moving onto Solana, the firm said.
Withdrawals resume
Binance began restoring withdrawals in phases at 1 a.m. ET on Sunday, and all 15 networks and assets in its first phase were available by 7:36 a.m. ET. In the first nine and a half hours, it processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, a net outflow of about $3.64 billion, the exchange said.
That represents 2.1% of the $171 billion in assets Binance reported in its most recent proof of reserves, from October 28, according to the exchange. "After an initial spike, withdrawal volumes have declined and are stabilising as expected," Binance said. It took a new reserves snapshot on October 31 and expects to publish an updated report on Monday.
As withdrawals began, CEO Richard Teng said Binance had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users," he wrote.
Today, we're beginning the phased resumption of withdrawals, taking a careful approach to ensure services return safely and securely.
We've now replenished approximately 95% of the impacted assets, and our commitment remains clear: Binance will absorb the financial impact of the… https://t.co/wKvI7Q4fsT pic.twitter.com/uWFGs3sJJ5
— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) November 1, 2026
Binance has since reopened withdrawals on more networks, including Zcash, TON and Sui, and on Monday restored fiat withdrawals in U.S. dollars, UAE dirhams, Vietnamese dong, Philippine pesos and Indonesian rupiah.
"Our top priority right now is to ensure the environment is secure, after which users can withdraw their funds and Binance can resume operations," Binance co-CEO Yi He said on X on Monday, Reuters reported. Binance said it has raised $6 billion to cover the losses from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and its SAFU emergency fund, according to Reuters, which also reported that Circle had frozen more than $1.1 billion in USDC.
Data from DefiLlama, which tracks the public wallets of exchanges, put Binance's total assets at about $127.6 billion on Monday. More than $6 billion left wallets associated with Binance over 24 hours after withdrawals reopened, CoinDesk reported, citing DefiLlama, though those movements can include transfers between Binance's own wallets. Rival exchanges OKX and Bybit recorded net inflows of about $450 million and $134 million, respectively, during Binance's reopening.
The hack has also rattled institutional investors. Spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $643.2 million on Friday, the first full trading session after the hack, leaving the funds with roughly $516 million in net outflows for October. "A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet," TRM Labs' Ari Redbord told Reuters.

瑞银：市场低估AI周期持续时间，2027年或迎投入回报拐点

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，据彭博社报道，瑞银首席欧洲股票策略师兼衍生品负责人 Gerry Fowler 表示，市场低估了 AI 周期的持续时间，AI 交易仍然稳健。他指出，一些超大规模云厂商的估值倍数已低于 20 倍，而营收仍每年增长 10% 至 20%，反映市场预期相当悲观，因此仍有不少投资者愿意重新买入 AI 相关资产。

Fowler 认为，巨额 AI 支出可能接近开始产生回报的阶段，2027 年或出现潜在拐点：数据中心交付有望释放积压订单，推动收入逐渐赶上资本开支。他表示，现金并未从市场消失，而是转移至存储芯片制造商等供应商，后者正开始向投资者返还现金。市场对存储芯片企业的定价，也反映了他认为过短的 AI 周期。

对于下一阶段受益者，Fowler 更关注帮助建设新工厂的全球及欧洲工业企业。他指出，许多电缆、电力设备等基础设施供应商的订单已排至 2027 年甚至 2028 年，盈利预测进一步上修的空间有限。ASML 则通过向三星电子、SK 海力士等扩产的存储厂商供应设备受益，而非直接供应数据中心；他表示，ASML 及欧洲部分工业企业正获得预期上修。

OpenRouter年化Token吞吐量突破1京，最近9周用量超过此前所有历史用量

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 模型聚合平台 OpenRouter 的 Token 消耗量再次暴涨。

10 月 26 日当周，平台处理了约 194 万亿 Token，折算年化吞吐量首次突破 1 京（10¹⁶）。

最近 9 周的处理量，超过了平台此前约 3 年 3 个月的总和。

推动增长的主要力量之一是 AI Agent。OpenRouter 官方数据显示，今年 2 月 6 日，Agent 的 Token 消耗首次超过人工交互。到 9 月最后一周，前者已经达到后者的约 7 倍。Agent 每执行一步，往往都要重新提交指令、工具定义和此前的操作记录。任务越长，反复处理的上下文就越多。

OpenRouter 的增长也吸引了支付巨头。Stripe 今年 8 月宣布收购该平台，希望将跨模型路由、Token 计费和成本优化整合起来。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Ezra Reguerra
items.content:
Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials
The HKMA plans to bring regulated stablecoins into tokenized government debt trials, while HSBC says its RedCoin stablecoin has reached 50,000 users.
Hong Kong has expanded its Project Ensemble pilot to allow round-the-clock settlement of tokenized transactions, as the city’s monetary regulator prepares to bring regulated stablecoins into trials involving tokenized government debt.
On Monday, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said that it had advanced its EnsembleTX project to a new stage allowing 24/7 real-value transactions. The HKMA said the update would help banks and their clients move funds globally, manage tokenized investments and handle treasury operations outside conventional settlement hours.
Participating banks initially settled payments through Hong Kong’s existing dollar settlement system, which limited settlement hours. When the pilot began real-value trials in November 2025, the HKMA said it planned to introduce tokenized central bank money to allow settlement around the clock.
The HKMA launched Project Ensemble in March 2024 to explore how banks could settle tokenized transactions using wholesale central bank digital money. A sandbox opened that August, allowing banks to connect their tokenized deposit platforms and test transactions.
Speaking at Hong Kong FinTech Week on Monday, HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said the regulator was introducing tokenized central bank money as a “foundation layer” for 24/7 settlement. He said tokenized bonds, money market funds and bank deposits were already being used.
The HKMA also said recognized dealers had completed secondary-market trial trades in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, a form of short-term debt issued by the regulator. It plans to expand those trials to include regulated stablecoins.
HSBC’s RedCoin reaches 50,000 users
Separately, HSBC Group CEO Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong FinTech Week that the bank’s recently launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin, had reached 50,000 users about 10 days after its debut.
“We have 50,000 users,” Elhedery said, adding that HSBC was targeting “multi-million users” as it expands access to the token.
RedCoin’s rollout brings stablecoins to retail payments, while Ensemble’s settlement work has focused on transactions involving banks and tokenized investments.
Elhedery said HSBC was also offering tokenized deposits to wholesale clients in Hong Kong and about half a dozen other jurisdictions, allowing funds to move around the clock.
Related: Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push
The bank launched RedCoin on Oct. 23 for transfers and merchant payments through its PayMe application. HSBC said more than 3.3 million PayMe customers could activate stablecoin wallets to use the token. It also plans to bring the stablecoin into its mobile banking app and allow subscriptions to tokenized investments, including a Hong Kong dollar money market fund share class.
HSBC was among Hong Kong’s first licensed stablecoin issuers in April alongside Anchorpoint Financial, a venture backed by Animoca Brands and Standard Chartered. The city’s licensing regime, introduced in August 2025, requires issuers to meet standards for backing reserves, redemption and risk management.
Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?
items.title: Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials

【印度央行与金融情报机构审查境外加密卡，多名用户反映卡片在印度无法使用】

Foresight News 消息，据《印度经济时报》援引两名知情人士报道，印度储备银行（RBI）和印度金融情报机构（FIU）正在关注境外加密卡的使用情况。这类卡片允许印度居民将加密货币兑换成卢比，用于境内消费和取现。报道称，过去几天内，部分印度居民的加密卡及服务商网站访问被屏蔽；自 10 月 29 日起，多名用户在社交媒体上反映其加密卡在印度无法使用。知情人士称，RBI 和 FIU 据悉正与 Visa、Mastercard 沟通此事，并不排除 Visa 等机构已开始停用印度境内或从印度发起的加密卡交易。RBI、Visa 和 Mastercard 均未回应置评请求。报道指出，此次屏蔽可能与印度非营利区块链研究机构 Digital South Trust 的提醒有关。该机构曾于 8 月申领一张由 Visa 支持的 RedotPay 虚拟加密卡，在印度境内完成多笔线上交易，并将相关记录提交给印度监管部门。报道及受访法律、税务专业人士认为，这类卡片可能违反印度《外汇管理法》（FEMA）及预付支付工具（PPI）、支付结算系统（PSS）相关监管框架。

Kimi进军游戏工业，让AI Agent接管从开发到运营的整条工作流

动察 Beating AI 快讯，月之暗面 Kimi 发布游戏开发与创意工作解决方案，试图让 AI Agent 从辅助编程走向游戏制作，参与从玩法设计、3D 建模、工程开发到发行运营的整条工作流。

这次 Kimi 不只是生成代码或美术素材，而是要直接进入游戏引擎干活。基于 K3.1 Pro、Kimi Code 和 Kimi Work，AI 可以通过插件操作 Unity、Unreal Engine、Blender 等专业工具，修改现有工程，甚至自己运行游戏、查看测试录像，发现问题后继续修改。

比如，策划只需提供参考图片、视频和玩法要求，Kimi 就能通过 Godot 制作包含挥剑、闪避、格挡等机制的 2.5D 动作游戏原型。官方称，即使没有编程经验，也有机会在 1–2 天内做出可试玩版本。另一次与 Unity 中国合作的演示中，Kimi 在没有人工干预的情况下连续工作 20 小时，复现原作并交付可继续开发的原生工程。

月之暗面还将目光投向游戏发行和长线运营：批量制作广告素材、分析玩家反馈、处理社区内容与本地化，甚至通过 API 为游戏 NPC 接入 AI 对话能力。

Key points:
- Kalshi traders put Democrats’ chances of winning control of the House at 93.6% ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections.
- US nonfarm payrolls are forecast to rise by 65,000 in October as markets favor a December Fed rate hike.
- Bitcoin holds its 100-day moving average as trader Rekt Capital compares its price chart with the 2023 recovery.
Midterms follow Bitcoin’s weakest October since 2014
Tuesday’s US midterm elections will determine control of Congress, with prediction market traders heavily favoring a Democratic victory in the House of Representatives.
Kalshi put the probability of Democrats winning the House at 93.6% as of Monday.
President Donald Trump said he would use his veto power if Democrats took control of Congress.
“I guess I’ll become Mr Veto. They’ll be sending stuff up. You veto it,” he said, according to the New York Post.
US midterm elections odds (screenshot). Source: Kalshi
Bitcoin ended the fourth quarter lower in each of the past three US midterm election years, falling 17.3% in 2014, 43.5% in 2018 and 14.8% in 2022. All three periods coincided with Bitcoin bear markets.
Benjamin Cowen, founder and CEO of crypto analytics platform IntoTheCryptoverse, suggested that the midterms can function as a cue to increase BTC exposure due to their short-term bearish impact on price.
“Usually the Q4 dump of midterm years just provide opportunities to buy for those who sold long ago,” he said Friday on X.
In July, Cowen referenced Bitcoin bear-market bottoms coinciding with the second half of midterm years.
BTC/USD was down 6.4% for the quarter as of Monday, after its weakest October since 2014, according to CoinGlass.
BTC/USD liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
Jobs data and tech earnings test market expectations
September US job openings data are due Tuesday, followed by October’s nonfarm payrolls report on Friday.
Payrolls are expected to rise by 65,000, after the economy added 29,000 jobs in September, below forecasts for 84,000. Such an outcome notionally increases the odds of dovish policy signals from the Federal Reserve, which is in turn bullish for crypto and risk-asset liquidity.
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Michelle Bowman are among the officials due to speak this week.
Data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool currently shows that markets expect the Fed to raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points at the December meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The odds of such an outcome have sat between 67% and 75% for the past month.
Fed target rate probability comparison for December FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
The University of Michigan will also release its preliminary November consumer sentiment survey on Friday, including consumers’ inflation expectations.
Alongside the macro data prints, 20% of S&P 500 companies are due to report earnings in the coming days. Chief among these are tech giants Apple and Palantir, both due to report after the market close on Monday.
The reports follow last week’s tech sell-off, when disappointing guidance renewed concerns about AI spending and profitability.
Economist Mohamed El-Erian described markets as now “acutely sensitive” to tech-sector news headlines in weekend analysis.
“The market is particularly focused on justification for the massive capital expenditures being deployed across the sector, ROI’s, and revenue growth,” he wrote.
Bitcoin chart draws comparisons with 2023 recovery
After closing October down 7.3%, Bitcoin is holding above a moving average that has provided support since mid-August.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
TradingView data showed BTC/USD staying above last week’s low near $76,300, without retesting it around the monthly close.
That low was close to the 100-day simple moving average (SMA) for BTC/USD, which has since risen to $76,548.
Bitcoin also reclaimed its 100-week exponential moving average (EMA) in time for the monthly close, with this standing at $77,759.
BTC/USD daily chart with 100 SMA, 100 EMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Trader and analyst Rekt Capital compared the weekly chart with Bitcoin’s rebound from its 2022 bear market low. During the recovery, BTC/USD produced an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, retested support at the right shoulder, briefly fell below it and then rallied.
Last week’s drop to $76,300 brought Bitcoin back to what Rekt Capital identified as right-shoulder support on the current chart. He is watching for a brief move below that level as a possible next step in the comparison.
“The question now is whether Bitcoin can produce some sort of downside deviation below here over the next few weeks,” Rekt Capital said.
BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com

I first released those in back in 2020 and now I finally added more architectures, Kernel selector, syscall descriptions and a few other niceties. It should work a bit better on mobile devices too but I am no CSS expert.

The API is at https://api.syscall.sh --- Top Comments --- [db48x]: It’s a side issue, but I’ve long thought that the kernel should duplicate every existing syscall that takes a null–terminated string by pointer with an otherwise identical syscall that takes the string by pointer, capacity, and length instead. It would be a huge boon to programs written in modern languages. I keep meaning to search the kernel mailing lists to see if the idea has been proposed before, but I never quite find the time. [ozgrakkurt]: Would also recommend using commands like: echo '#include <sys/syscall.h>' | gcc -E -dM -xc - | grep -i "read" To get the real values on your PC to make sure. I had LLMs give wrong numbers or constant definitions several times but getting it to generate a command like this and seeing it for myself works every time. Also chromium docs has a table: https://www.chromium.org/chromium-os/developer-library/refer... It would be very useful to ... [bkallus]: On x86_64 and x32, the syscall number goes in eax, not rax. The upper 32 bits of rax are ignored and can be anything. [guitmz]: I also made a CLI for consulting the syscall API when I originally released the website. I think I can tidy up the code and make it public too. It uses a embedded dataset so it does not have to query the API endpoint all the time [DustinBrett]: That website messes with my graphics for some reason.

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，分析师 Axel Adler Jr. 表示，截至 11 月 1 日，比特币活跃地址 30 日均值约 62.9 万，较 2024 年 12 月本地峰值约 110 万下降 43%，过去一周再降 1%，目前较全年均值约 70.2 万低约 10%。2018 年该指标曾从约 110 万降至约 54.7 万、降幅约 50%，但历时约三个月，本轮自峰值回落已近两年，幅度相近但收缩更慢。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Zoltan Vardai
items.content:
OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B
OKX led cryptocurrency exchanges with $445 million in daily inflows, while Binance processed about $7 billion in net outflows.
OKX recorded about $445 million in 24-hour net inflows, the largest among tracked crypto exchanges, while Binance continued to register outflows after reopening withdrawals following its $6.3 billion hack.
Crypto exchange Bybit was in second place with $112 million in net inflows, followed by Gate with $91 million and Bitget with $54 million in 24-hour net inflows, according to DefiLlama.
Binance recorded the biggest net outflows among tracked exchanges, with more than $7 billion, up from $5.8 billion earlier Monday. Binance said it began restoring withdrawals in phases at 6:00 a.m. UTC on Sunday.
At the time of writing, Binance held about $127.9 billion in wallets tracked by DefiLlama, more than four times the $29 billion at OKX, the second-largest exchange by that measure.
Binance suspended withdrawals Friday, soon after late Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack, the largest in cryptocurrency history.
By Sunday, Binance said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% on Saturday. The remaining 5% consisted of less liquid tokens that it continued to buy through market and over-the-counter transactions.
The exchange is using its corporate treasury, a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and a portion of its futures insurance fund to replace the stolen assets. Binance has pledged to absorb the losses without passing them on to customers.
About $3 billion in stolen assets frozen by industry partners is separate from Binance’s replacement funds. Binance said Sunday it published a new reserves snapshot and an updated proof-of-reserves report was expected Monday.
OKX’s OKB token rose about 1.4% over the past 24 hours to trade near $113 on Monday, while BNB gained 0.3% to about $708 over the same period, according to CoinMarketCap.
Related: THORChain’s RUNE jumps 13% after Binance’s record $6.3B hack

韩媒：三星计划在2030年前完全退出8英寸晶圆代工业务

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 2 日，根据韩国科技媒体 TheElec 的报道，三星电子计划在 2030 年前完全退出 8 英寸晶圆代工业务，将战略重心全面转向利润更高的 12 英寸先进制程。

报道指出，三星将逐步缩减其 8 英寸产线。其中，位于器兴园区的 S7 工厂计划在 2026 年下半年率先关闭，该厂月产能约为 5 万片晶圆。S7 关闭后，三星 8 英寸晶圆的总月产能将从 25 万片降至 20 万片以下。剩余 S6 和 S8 工厂的产能利用率当时已降至约 70%。三星代工业务负责人韩镇万（Han Jin-man）此前也曾表示，8 英寸代工市场竞争已变得「日益拥挤且由价格驱动」，公司计划逐步缩减该业务。

items.content:
阿里云推出Qovest：99元/月起，给投资者配个「超级投研助手」

动察 Beating AI 快讯，阿里云发布 AI 投研工作台 Qovest，面向专业投资者。用户只需提出研究需求，它就能自动查询金融数据、搜集财报资料、拆解产业链、测算投资规模，最终生成研究报告。

比如，研究人形机器人产业链，它能拆解各环节的单机价值和国产化水平，生成可交互的产业链图谱。研究数据中心电力设施，只需修改一个前提假设，相关测算就能自动更新。

Qovest 还提供「投研空间」，可以保存历史研究成果、操盘笔记和待验证问题，让用户不必每次都从头开始研究。它还支持定时追踪市场变化。用户可以为黄金 ETF 设置每周研究任务，让 AI 定期更新国际金价、美元指数、ETF 持仓和央行购金等数据，并生成动态分析看板。

为了提高金融研究的准确性，阿里云采购了专业金融数据库，并自研金融 Agent 执行框架，打通数据调用、分析和报告生成流程。官方称，Qovest 在 FinFIRST 和 iRaB 两套金融评测集的内部横评中，回答质量、响应速度和成本均领先，但尚未公开具体成绩和测试配置。

目前 Qovest 已面向个人用户开放邀测，注册可领取积分免费试用，后续提供每月 99 元和 199 元两档订阅套餐。面向金融机构的企业版也计划近期推出。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/374999
